papers.title: The Mediating Role of Sleep Quality in Associations of Smartphone Addiction and Time-Specific Use With Prenatal Depression and Anxiety: Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
papers.abstract: Prenatal depression and anxiety have emerged as pressing global public health challenges. In the digital era, excessive smartphone use may exert complex effects on maternal mental health. Prior research has predominantly focused on adolescents, whereas evidence among pregnant women, particularly regarding total weekly use and use during critical circadian windows, such as after waking and before bedtime, remains limited. Furthermore, the mediating role of sleep quality in these associations has yet to be systematically examined. This study aimed to investigate the associations of smartphone addiction and time-specific smartphone use with prenatal depression and anxiety, and to assess the mediating role of sleep quality in these associations. This cross-sectional observational study enrolled 537 pregnant women. Smartphone use characteristics, sleep quality, and prenatal depression and anxiety were assessed using the Smartphone Addiction Scale-Short Version (SAS-SV), objective total weekly smartphone use recorded by the device, and self-reported duration of smartphone use after waking and duration of bedtime smartphone use; the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), respectively. Binary logistic regression was used to estimate associations, restricted cubic spline (RCS) models were used to explore nonlinear patterns, and exploratory mediation analyses were used to examine whether sleep quality statistically accounted for part of the observed associations. The prevalence of moderate-to-severe prenatal depression and anxiety was 8.8% (47/537) and 5.8% (31/537), respectively. After adjusting for covariates, smartphone addiction was associated with higher odds of depression (odds ratio [OR] 3.461, 95% CI 1.771-7.100) and anxiety (OR 7.738, 95% CI 3.064-23.172). Duration of smartphone use after waking ≥61 minutes and duration of bedtime smartphone use ≥91 minutes were also associated with higher odds of affective disorders. RCS analyses further revealed distinct nonlinear patterns across different exposure dimensions: duration of smartphone use after waking displayed U-shaped and J-shaped associations with depression and anxiety, respectively, while total weekly use displayed a U-shaped association with anxiety. Exploratory mediation analyses showed that the indirect pathways through sleep quality were statistically significant for the associations of bedtime smartphone use, weekly smartphone use, and smartphone addiction with prenatal depression, with mediation proportions of 44.89% (0.0065/0.0145), 31.30% (0.0056/0.0183), and 31.48% (0.0415/0.1315), respectively. The corresponding proportions in the anxiety models were 35.83% (0.0044/0.0123), 27.05% (0.0039/0.0144), and 22.73% (0.0271/0.1187). Smartphone addiction and excessive smartphone use after waking and before bedtime were associated with higher odds of prenatal depression and anxiety. Sleep quality may statistically account for part of these associations, but longitudinal studies are needed to establish temporal ordering and causal pathways.

papers.title: Comparison of Albino and Pigmented Rat Oxygen-Induced Retinopathy Models: From Vascular to Neural Retinal Changes.
papers.abstract: To compare two commonly used rat models of oxygen-induced retinopathy (OIR)-the 50/10 model in Sprague-Dawley rats and the 80/40 model in Long-Evans rats-to identify which more closely reproduces the features of human retinopathy. Dams and pups were exposed from postnatal day 0 (P0) to P14 to alternating oxygen cycles, followed by analyses at P14, P18, and P28. The 50/10 protocol alternated 50% and 10% oxygen every 24 hours, whereas the 80/40 protocol alternated 80% and 40% oxygen every 12 hours. The vascular, structural, and functional retinal changes were assessed using in vivo imaging and electrophysiology, as well as ex vivo histological and molecular analyses. Both OIR protocols induced significant retinal vascular abnormalities compared with controls, but with marked differences in onset, severity, and persistence. The 50/10 protocol produced earlier and more sustained vascular alterations, including reduced vascular coverage, increased vascular tortuosity, and neovascularization beginning at P14. Similar vascular changes appeared later and were less persistent in the 80/40 model. Retinal thinning occurred in both models; however, long-term photoreceptor segment thinning was observed only in the 50/10 protocol. The 50/10 protocol was associated with increased retinal cell death, significant cone photoreceptor loss, and mostly reduced electroretinographic responses, findings that were not observed in the 80/40 protocol. Both OIR models replicate features of human pathology, but differ in disease dynamics. These differences should be considered when selecting an OIR protocol, depending on whether vascular pathology or neurodegeneration is the primary therapeutic target.

papers.title: Sociodemographic and lifestyle correlates of accelerometer-measured 24-hour physical behavior patterns: a cross-sectional analysis of the ELSA-Brasil cohort.
papers.abstract: Physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep comprise an integrated 24-hour movement continuum that may influence health outcomes. While these behaviors have been studied separately, limited evidence exists on their combined patterns and related sociodemographic and lifestyle factors in middle-income countries like Brazil. The objective was to evaluate associations between sociodemographic and lifestyle correlates and accelerometer-measured 24-hour physical behavior patterns among Brazilian middle-aged and older adults. This cross-sectional analysis included 9,520 adults (mean age 59.2 ± 8.6 years) from the third wave of the ELSA-Brasil cohort study. Physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep were objectively measured using triaxial hip-worn accelerometers for seven consecutive days. Behavioral clusters were defined according to daily time spent in physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep using Partitioning Around Medoids cluster analysis. Sociodemographic and lifestyle factors were assessed via standardized questionnaires. Multinomial logistic regression models evaluated associations between correlates and behavioral clusters, with Cluster 3 as the reference category. Three clusters were identified: 1 (lower physical activity, higher sedentary behavior, shorter sleep), 2 (intermediate physical activity, intermediate sedentary behavior, intermediate sleep), and 3 (higher physical activity, lower sedentary behavior, longer sleep). Compared with Cluster 3, participants in Cluster 1 were more likely to be male, to have a higher body mass index, to have higher educational attainment, and to have a high income. Similar but weaker associations were observed for Cluster 2. Distinct 24-hour physical behavior patterns among Brazilian adults were associated with sociodemographic and lifestyle factors. These cross-sectional findings emphasize the need for targeted public health strategies promoting healthier 24-hour behavior profiles.

papers.title: EEG-Based Cognitive Overload-Driven Adaptive Training for Enhancing Performance Under Simulated High-Stress Space Operation Tasks.
papers.abstract: Given the potential for highly complex and high-risk space operation tasks to induce cognitive overload in operators, effective training is crucial for maintaining mission performance and safety. Conventional adaptive training often struggles to balance task challenge while preventing overload. To address this limitation, this study proposes an EEG-based cognitive overload-driven adaptive training method that integrates hybrid feature selection, Normalized Fast Dynamic Time Warping (NFDTW)-based feature alignment and a shared knowledge layer to improve online cognitive overload detection under nonstationary conditions. A dual-factor task regulation strategy combining task performance and cognitive overload states is further developed to adjust task difficulty based on these two factors. The results showed that the proposed detection method achieved online detection accuracies of 92.07% and 84.67% on the two datasets, respectively, with maximum relative improvements of 7.74% and 8.34% over the comparison methods. The adaptive training strategy was further evaluated in a VR-based robotic arm docking task involving three groups: fixed, control, and adaptive. Mixed-design ANOVA showed that the adaptive group exhibited significant improvements in task performance and SAS as well as more favorable changes in EEG features. Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons further revealed significant group differences ([Formula: see text]). These findings demonstrate the feasibility of EEG-based cognitive overload-driven adaptive training for complex space operation scenarios.

papers.title: Salivary Gene Expression and Systemic Inflammatory Markers in Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Periodontal Disease.
papers.abstract: To evaluate whether periodontal status modulates systemic low-grade inflammation and the expression of salivary molecular biomarkers in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). A cross-sectional observational study was conducted in 113 patients distributed into three groups: periodontitis (n=52), OSA with periodontitis (n=30), and OSA without periodontitis (n=31). Systemic inflammatory markers were analyzed in peripheral blood, including interleukin-6 (IL-6), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (CRP), fibrinogen, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), platelet-to-leukocyte ratio (PLR), and high-density lipoprotein (HDL). Salivary mRNA expression of leptin (LEP), leptin receptor (LEPR), and C-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CCL2) was determined by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). Associations between biomarkers, periodontal parameters, and OSA severity were assessed. Patients with OSA and periodontitis showed significantly higher levels of IL-6 (p<0.001) and fibrinogen (p<0.05), whereas CRP showed an increasing trend without reaching statistical significance. In patients with OSA, salivary LEP mRNA expression was negatively correlated with the oxygen desaturation index (ODI) (r = -0.627; p = 0.044). A trend toward increased salivary expression of LEP, LEPR, and CCL2 was observed in the presence of periodontal disease. The coexistence of OSA and periodontal disease is associated with a more pronounced systemic inflammatory profile and a trend toward altered expression of salivary biomarkers.

papers.title: Pragmatic trial of a self-directed intervention for weight loss in obstructive sleep apnea (POWER).
papers.abstract: Self-directed lifestyle interventions may improve access to weight loss care in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but effectiveness in routine practice is unknown. Test whether a proactively delivered self-directed lifestyle intervention improves weight and sleep-related quality of life versus usual care. POWER enrolled patients with OSA and body mass index of 30-45 kg/m2, recruited from Veteran Affairs (VA) sites nationwide, and randomized participants to a self-directed intervention based on the Diabetes Prevention Program with video-based sessions, readings, and regular coaching reminders or usual care. Co-primary outcomes were change in Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire (FOSQ) and clinical weight in kilograms (kg) from baseline to 12 months post-randomization. Given two primary outcomes, we defined significance at p = 0.025. This trial randomized 696 participants. Mean age was 56.2 years (SD 12.2), with 19.7% identifying as female. Clinical weights at 12 months were available for 81.9% of intervention and 83.6% of control participants. Unadjusted weight declined 2.1 kg (SD 6.8) in intervention and 0.9 kg (SD 5.9) in control (adjusted between-group difference: -1.1 kg, 95%CI -2.0, -0.1; p = 0.037). FOSQ measures were available at 12 months for 78.2% of intervention and 90.5% of control participants. From baseline to 12 months, unadjusted FOSQ improved 1.4 (SD 2.7) points in intervention and 0.9 (SD 2.9) points in control (adjusted between-group difference: 0.6 points, 95%CI 0.2, 1.0; p = 0.001). Among participants with OSA and obesity, a self-directed lifestyle intervention did not improve weight loss and led to improvements in sleep-related quality of life that are of limited clinical importance. Clinicaltrials.gov NCT05104450, registered 10/19/2021.

papers.title: Transcriptional coordination of the aromatic amino acid metabolic network in Petunia and beyond.
papers.abstract: Plants produce vast arrays of specialized metabolites mediating ecological interactions, notably including phenylalanine-derived metabolites. Biosynthesizing these metabolites requires not only defined structural pathways, but also tight coordination between the shikimate pathway, aromatic amino acid production, and downstream specialized metabolism, such as benzenoid metabolism. Regulation occurs at multiple levels, including post-translational control of enzymes through mechanisms such as allostery, wherein binding of a regulatory metabolite alters catalytic activity. However, transcriptional regulation is also a flux control mechanism in these pathways and has increasingly been studied. Here, we summarize recent developments in this field. Petunia emerged as a key model for understanding how transcriptional networks regulate this metabolic system, complemented by discoveries in other species. Central to this regulation are MYB transcription factors, including PhODO1, PhEOBI, and PhEOBII, which coordinate the expression of genes involved in both precursor supply and volatile formation. These regulators operate within broad networks that integrate environmental signals, including light, circadian rhythms, temperature, and hormonal cues, through additional transcription factors. Developmental regulators, particularly MADS-box transcription factors, link floral organ identity with metabolism, ensuring scent production occurs within appropriate developmental stages and tissues. Beyond transcriptional and enzymatic regulation, accumulation and utilization are also influenced by post-synthetic processes, including glycosylation, intracellular sequestration, transport, storage, and export. Together, these elements form multilayered frameworks that coordinates primary and specialized metabolism, ultimately determining composition, accumulation, and utilization of specialized metabolites. Expanding this framework across plant species will be essential for understanding metabolic regulation and enabling targeted manipulation of aroma and stress-related traits in crops.

papers.title: Acupuncture for Symptoms Characteristic of the Fatigue-Sleep Disturbance-Depression Symptom Cluster (FSDSC) in Breast Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: BackgroundThis study aimed to evaluate the effects of acupuncture or acupressure on fatigue, sleep disturbance/insomnia, and depression, the three component symptoms within the fatigue-sleep disturbance-depression symptom-cluster (FSDSC) conceptual framework in patients with breast cancer.MethodsA systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Seven databases (Embase, MEDLINE [Ovid], Cochrane Library [Trials], Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, CNKI, and Wanfang Data) were searched from inception to June 2025 without language restrictions. Eligible randomized controlled trials evaluated acupuncture or acupressure for at least one prespecified component symptom. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Meta-analyses were conducted using RevMan 5.4. PROSPERO: CRD42024608618.ResultsTwenty-one trials involving 2,153 participants were included. Meta-analysis showed significant improvements in fatigue measured by the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI: -9.73; 95% CI, -18.03 to -1.43; p=0.02) and Brief Fatigue Inventory (BFI: -1.13; 95% CI, -1.79 to -0.47; p=0.0008). Sleep quality improved according to the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI: -2.43; 95% CI, -3.45 to -1.42; p<0.0001) and insomnia severity according to the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI: -1.05; 95% CI, -1.74 to -0.36; p=0.003). Depression (-1.34; 95% CI, -2.08 to -0.60; P = 0.0004) and quality of life measured by FACT-B (8.10; 95% CI, 6.47 to 9.72; P < 0.0001) also significantly improved.ConclusionsAcupuncture or acupressure may improve symptoms related to the FSDSC conceptual framework in patients with breast cancer. These findings support its potential role in managing co-occurring symptoms, although further high-quality trials are warranted.

papers.title: Association of the six-minute walk test with severity of obstructive sleep apnea: an observational study.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) impairs sleep quality and exercise capacity through intermittent hypoxia and autonomic dysfunction. Simple tools that correlate objective exercise tolerance with OSA severity remain underutilized in clinical practice. The study aimed to find the association between 6-minute walk test (6MWT) performance and polysomnographic severity indices in patients with newly diagnosed OSA and whether functional exercise parameters can predict OSA severity. This cross-sectional observational study was conducted at a tertiary care center between July 2023 and January 2025. A total of 124 consecutive adults (age ≥18 years) with newly diagnosed OSA diagnosed from level I polysomnography (PSG) underwent standardized 6MWT as per American Thoracic Society Guidelines within one week of PSG testing. Primary endpoints included 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), oxygen saturation changes, post-test Borg dyspnea scale, and heart rate recovery at 1, 2, and 3 minutes. Correlations with Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) and Oxygen Desaturation Index (ODI) were analyzed using Spearman's correlation, multiple linear regression, and one-way analysis of variance with Games-Howell post-hoc testing. The study included 124 participants (85.5% male, mean age 46±11.3 years, mean body mass index 33.19±5.9 kg/m²), of whom 79.8% were participants with severe OSA. Mean AHI and ODI were 52.25±23.69 and 54.04±29.22 events/hour, respectively. Mean 6MWD decreased significantly across OSA severity groups: mild 420.85±17.4 m, moderate 396.99±9.60 m, and severe 348.61±22.01 m. Strong negative correlations were found between AHI and 6MWD (ρ=-0.974, p<0.001) and ODI and 6MWD (ρ=-0.775, p<0.001). Multiple linear regression results in two important predictive models: AHI=258.65+[(0.58×Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS)] + (1.89×Borg dyspnea post-6MWT) - (0.1×6MWD) and ODI=207.88+(0.96×ESS) + (4.21×Borg dyspnea post-6MWT) - (0.51×6MWD). As measured by the 6MWT, functional exercise capacity is strongly and inversely associated with the severity of OSA. The derived regression equations serve as a valuable, practical adjunct for assessing the functional impairment and hypoxic burden in patients with OSA, particularly in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Beyond the apnea-hypopnea index: clinical phenotypic heterogeneity of obstructive sleep apnea in an Indian tertiary referral cohort using level III polysomnography.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is usually classified by a single severity index, the Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI), which does not capture the clinical heterogeneity described in other populations. To characterize clinically distinct OSA phenotypes by body habitus, symptom-severity relationship, and by respiratory event type in an Indian tertiary referral cohort, using level III polysomnography. Retrospective analysis of 309 patients with OSA (AHI≥5) from consecutive level III polysomnography studies at a tertiary Indian center. Phenotypes were defined as follows: 1) lean [body mass index (BMI)<25 kg/m²] versus non-lean OSA; 2) symptomatic vs. asymptomatic disease, using an Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) score of 10 as a threshold, crossed with AHI severity; 3) apnea-predominant vs. hypopnea-predominant disease, from the respective event indices. An exploratory unsupervised cluster analysis on physiological variables was performed as a comparator. A lean phenotype was present in 12.3% of patients (95% confidence interval 9.1-16.5) and had lower AHI, less hypoxemia, and fewer daytime symptoms than non-lean OSA, with less moderate-to-severe disease (40.5% vs. 68.4%, p=0.002). Symptom burden was poorly matched to severity: 52.7% of severe OSA patients were not sleepy (ESS<10), while 21.5% of mild OSA patients were. Sleepy patients had a greater hypoxemic burden but similar body habitus. Apnea-predominant disease (54.3% of patients with usable indices) occurred in younger, leaner patients but with a higher AHI than hypopnea-predominant disease. Both the lean-phenotype association with less severe disease and the apnea-predominant AHI difference persisted after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI. STOP-Bang score did not reliably discriminate moderate-to-severe disease in this already high-risk referral population (AUC 0.56), and hypertension and diabetes prevalence did not differ between lean and non-lean phenotypes. ODI graded on AHI's own thresholds agreed with the AHI category in 67.4% of patients (quadratic-weighted κ 0.82) and identified moderate-to-severe disease with 89% sensitivity and 92% specificity. Unsupervised clustering on AHI-correlated physiological variables did not identify phenotypes independent of severity. OSA in this referral cohort separates into body-habitus, symptom-discordance and event-type phenotypes that are not interchangeable with AHI severity alone. Recognizing these patterns may help identify lean patients, underrecognized asymptomatic severe disease, and mechanistically distinct event patterns.

papers.title: Motor memory consolidation during sleep after stroke: the rehabilitation timing hypothesis.
papers.abstract: Motor recovery after stroke depends on neuroplasticity-driven reorganisation of surviving cortical circuits. A growing body of evidence implicates sleep as an active consolidator of motor memories acquired during rehabilitation. Yet stroke disrupts the very sleep architecture required for this process, and current clinical practice schedules rehabilitation without regard for its temporal proximity to sleep. This review synthesizes the mechanistic, preclinical, and emerging clinical evidence underlying the rehabilitation timing hypothesis. Sleep spindles, nested within slow oscillations during NREM sleep, are a principal electrophysiological substrate for motor memory consolidation, and emerging evidence implicates cerebellar-cortical dynamics during spindles. Stroke disrupts this oscillatory coupling through lesion-related alterations in thalamocortical circuitry, GABAergic signalling, and interhemispheric synchrony. Preclinical studies demonstrate that optogenetically-enhanced slow waves during sleep accelerate motor recovery, while pharmacological GABA modulation restores consolidation-promoting oscillations. Chronobiological evidence from healthy adults and older populations suggests that evening training followed by nocturnal sleep may produce superior long-term motor retention compared with morning training. The rehabilitation timing hypothesis is plausible and clinically testable, but direct evidence in stroke populations is currently lacking. Scheduling motor therapy close to sleep is a low-cost strategy that warrants formal evaluation as a means of enhancing stroke recovery. Formal clinical trials testing therapy timing as an independent variable are urgently needed.

papers.title: Depth-adaptive suppression of subject-dependent interference for robust cross-subject EEG emotion recognition.
papers.abstract: Cross-subject electroencephalography (EEG) emotion recognition is limited by inter-subject variability, which embeds subject-specific nuisance information in learned representations and reduces generalization to unseen individuals. We propose a two-stage layer-adaptive subject-interference suppression framework built on EEG Conformer. In the search stage, differentiable gates and adversarial subject classifiers are attached to hierarchical representations from the patch embedding layer and Transformer blocks to estimate where subject information is most strongly encoded. The top-ranked layers are then fixed and the model is retrained for final emotion classification. A subject-aware supervised contrastive regularizer is further used to improve label-consistent cross-subject representation learning. Experiments on SEED under strict leave-one-subject-out evaluation show improved performance over representative machine-learning, domain-adaptation, and deep-learning baselines. Auxiliary experiments on SEED-IV indicate adaptability under a more challenging label setting. Layer-wise probing shows that subject-specific information remains decodable across depths but is relatively stronger in shallow and early intermediate representations. Selective depth-aware suppression provides a practical and interpretable strategy for robust EEG-based affective brain-computer interfaces.

papers.title: PHYA and PHYC as Candidate Loci for Flowering Time and Developmental Plasticity in Wheat.
papers.abstract: Plant architecture and developmental timing are influenced by light availability, especially in high-density cropping systems, where canopy shading modifies both light intensity and spectral quality. Despite their ecological and agronomical importance, the genetic basis of these responses in wheat remains poorly understood. Here, using a Recombinant Inbred Lines (RILs) population, we investigated phenological and morphological traits under sunlight and simulated canopy shade. We identified a major QTL on chromosome 5A with light-dependent allelic effects, indicating genotype-by-environment variation in developmental responses. This QTL corresponds to a structural rearrangement, consistent with an inversion in the wild emmer reference genome that suppresses recombination and maintains a haplotype block at a flowering locus including PHYTOCHROME C (PHYC-A) and VERNALIZATION-1 (VRN-A1). Analysis of a tetraploid wheat diversity panel further showed that natural variation at PHYC-A interacted with VRN-A1 to regulate heading time, with the effect of PHYC-A being substantially stronger in winter VRN-A1 backgrounds. This epistatic interaction likely reflects PHYC's role in modulating the circadian phase of photoperiod-pathway genes. Additionally, we found an early stop codon in the BB genome copy of PHYTOCHROME A (PHYA-B) on chromosome 4B associated with delayed heading, supported by TILLING-derived phytochrome mutants that reveal distinct and complementary roles for PHYA and PHYC in regulating flowering time, plant height, and leaf elongation under simulated canopy shade. Our findings highlight the potential contribution of phytochrome variation to wheat development under canopy-like light environment, thereby extending model insights to agronomically relevant conditions.

papers.title: Delayed Recognition of Autism Spectrum Disorder and Off-Label Lurasidone After Intolerance to Risperidone and Aripiprazole in a Latin American Child: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) can be difficult to recognize when co-occurring psychiatric symptoms are more clinically prominent, which may delay diagnosis. We report the case of a nine-year-old Latin American boy whose ASD and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) were not diagnosed until approximately 27 months after initial presentation with irritability, mood lability, anxiety, and, subsequently, hallucinatory experiences; these symptoms were initially managed as primary psychiatric conditions. During this interval, fluoxetine was discontinued due to symptom worsening, sertraline produced only partial benefit, and both Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved agents for irritability associated with autistic disorder were discontinued because of adverse effects: risperidone due to significant weight gain and aripiprazole due to nausea, vomiting, and dizziness. A detailed neurodevelopmental reassessment subsequently identified longstanding social communication difficulties, rigid routines, sensory sensitivities, and restricted interests, supporting diagnoses of ASD and OCD. Low-dose lurasidone (20 mg nightly) was initiated off-label alongside continued sertraline. Over the following year, the patient demonstrated sustained improvement in irritability, aggression, self-injurious behavior, anxiety, and sleep disturbance. Hallucinatory experiences resolved within approximately three months and did not recur, with no significant adverse effects observed. This case illustrates how more prominent psychiatric symptoms can mask ASD and describes the individualized use of off-label lurasidone after intolerance to approved agents. However, the temporal association with clinical improvement does not establish causality, and findings from a single case cannot demonstrate efficacy.

papers.title: Assessment of Compliance With the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence Guidance in the Management of Patients Referred Following a First Suspected Seizure: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.
papers.abstract: Introduction A first suspected seizure requires timely specialist assessment and appropriate investigation to establish an accurate diagnosis, identify seizure mimics, assess the risk of recurrence, and provide appropriate safety advice. The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidance recommends urgent specialist assessment following a first suspected seizure, alongside appropriate electrocardiography, electroencephalography, neuroimaging, recurrence-risk assessment, and patient safety advice. This audit evaluated adherence to these standards within a first-seizure clinic. Materials and methods A retrospective clinical audit was undertaken on patients referred to a first-seizure clinic from the Emergency Department and Acute Medicine Unit over a three-month period from January to March 2025. Data were obtained from electronic patient records, clinic correspondence, and discharge documentation. Compliance with predefined standards from NICE guidance was assessed. The primary outcome measures were timely specialist assessment, 12-lead electrocardiography, documentation of individualized seizure recurrence risk, timely electroencephalography where clinically indicated, timely neuroimaging where indicated, and documentation of safety-netting and driving advice. Results Sixty-three patient records were initially identified. Ten patients did not attend or were lost to follow-up and were excluded from the final clinical analysis, leaving 53 patients. Five of 53 patients (9.4%) received specialist assessment within two weeks. A 12-lead ECG was documented in all 53 patients (100%), and an individualized seizure recurrence risk assessment was documented in all patients (100%). An electroencephalogram (EEG) was indicated in 17 patients, of whom one (5.9%) underwent EEG within 72 hours; 15 (88.2%) underwent EEG after 72 hours, and one patient did not attend. The mean time to EEG among those who eventually underwent the investigation was approximately 12.5 weeks. Neuroimaging was indicated in 41 patients, of whom 22 (53.7%) underwent imaging within six weeks and 19 (46.3%) underwent imaging after six weeks. Safety-netting, including documentation of driving/Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) advice, was documented in all 53 patients (100%). Conclusion The audit demonstrated high compliance with core assessment and documentation standards but substantial delays in specialist review and time-critical investigations. The greatest gap was in timely EEG access, followed by delays in specialist assessment and neuroimaging. The findings support service-level interventions aimed at improving urgent access to first-seizure assessment and investigations. A repeat audit, following the implementation of targeted interventions, will be important to determine whether pathway changes improve compliance.

papers.title: Network-Informed Health-Burden Profiles Among Older Adults with Symptomatic Knee Osteoarthritis Phenotype: A Latent Class Analysis.
papers.abstract: Older adults with symptomatic knee osteoarthritis (KOA) may exhibit heterogeneous combinations of functional limitation, psychological burden, perceived health, comorbidity burden, and multisite pain. This study aimed to identify network-informed key indicators and derive clinically interpretable, management-oriented health-burden profiles to support multidimensional assessment and future preference-sensitive care research. In this cross-sectional secondary analysis, we analyzed 2011 baseline data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) among adults aged 60 years or older with physician-diagnosed arthritis or rheumatism and knee pain. Eighteen indicators were modeled using an extended Bayesian information criterion graphical lasso network based on mixed-scale correlations. Three structural metrics were integrated to prioritize indicators, and the prioritized indicators were entered into latent class analysis (LCA). Multinomial logistic regression examined profile correlates. Robustness was assessed across five multiply imputed datasets, after removing diabetes from the LCA, and in an exploratory 2018 later-wave reproducibility analysis. Among 749 participants, depressive symptoms, poor self-rated health, instrumental and basic activities of daily living limitations, diabetes, and non-knee pain burden ranked highest. Although the two-class model had the lowest Bayesian information criterion (BIC), the three-class model had the lowest sample-size-adjusted BIC (aBIC), acceptable classification quality, adequate minimum class size, and greater clinical interpretability. Profiles reflected lower overall health burden (n=93, 12.4%), psychological-perceived health burden (n=312, 41.7%), and multidimensional high-burden functional limitation (n=344, 45.9%). Rural residence, greater comorbidity burden, and sleep disturbance were associated with higher-burden profiles. The 2018 analysis (n=2280) yielded three broadly analogous qualitative profiles, although class proportions, some item-response patterns, and classification certainty differed from 2011. Network-informed LCA identified three multidimensional health-burden profiles, with partial later-wave reproducibility. These profiles may inform multidimensional assessment and future stratified, preference-sensitive care research but require confirmation in independent clinical cohorts with direct measures of preference, treatment acceptability, and adherence.

papers.title: Real-World Classification of Pain States in Multiple Sclerosis Patients using Wearable Sensor Data and Ensemble Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Pain assessment remains challenging due to its subjective nature and reliance on self-reports. These challenges are particularly relevant for multiple sclerosis (MS) patients, for whom pain is among the most common and fluctuating symptoms, occurring in multiple forms. Wearable sensors combined with machine learning (ML) offer the potential for continuous and more objective pain monitoring by leveraging physiological signals in real-world contexts. We monitored 18 MS patients over 48 h using the Empatica E4 wristband to collect photoplethysmography, electrodermal activity, skin temperature, and accelerometer data. Physiological features were extracted from 5-, 10-, and 15-min time windows preceding hourly self-reported pain assessment during waking hours. Univariate associations with pain states were evaluated using linear mixed effects models, correcting for multiple comparisons. For classification purposes, feature selection was performed via recursive feature elimination, and 5 ML algorithms were trained and tested with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. Model performance was evaluated using the F1 score and the sensitivity-specificity balance. For univariate analysis, after correction, only 2 out of 43 features showed significant differences between pain and no-pain states. For the classification task, models based on 5-min windows generally performed the best. The highest F1 score (0.78) was achieved by a Support Vector Machine using 2 features from 5-min windows, while XGBoost achieved the best sensitivity-specificity balance (0.69/0.68) with 2 features from 15-min windows. Wearable physiological signals may contain information relevant to pain-state classification in people with MS. However, these results should be considered preliminary, requiring validation in larger, independent cohorts to establish the robustness and generalizability of the proposed approach.

papers.title: The moderating role of anger rumination and self-control in the day-to-day associations between irritability and sleep in male adolescents: An exploratory experience sampling method study.
papers.abstract: Irritability is highly prevalent in adolescents and may be exacerbated by sleep disturbances, with sleep patterns undergoing significant changes during this developmental period. Reciprocally, poor sleep may generate an increase in anger dysregulation. This exploratory study investigates the day-to-day associations between sleep and irritability, as well as the moderating effects of maladaptive (i.e., anger rumination) and adaptive (i.e., self-control) emotion regulation (ER) strategies. Fifty-six male adolescents aged 12-18, with diverse sleep and emotional problems, participated in a 9-day experience sampling method study. Participants also completed self-report questionnaires assessing irritability, sleep quantity and quality, and maladaptive and adaptive ER strategies. Linear mixed effect models with lagged covariates were used to test associations and moderating effects. At the within-person level, sleep quality was associated with next-day irritability (βstd = -0.92, 95% CI [-1.31, -0.53). Higher daily anger rumination (βstd = 0.25, 95% CI [0.17, 0.34]), and daily self-control (βstd = -0.18, 95% CI [-0.27, -0.10]) were directly associated with higher next-day irritability. At the between-person level, lower self-control was also associated with higher next-day irritability (βstd = -0.52, 95% CI [-0.77, -0.27]). Interactions between daily sleep quality and between-person anger rumination ( β std interaction = 0.18, 95% [0.07, 0.30]), and self-control ( β std interaction = 0.75, 95% CI [0.38, 1.12]) were related with irritability. Reciprocally, lower irritability from the day was associated with better sleep quality the following night (βstd = -0.11, 95% CI [-0.20, -0.01]). These preliminary findings suggest that sleep may be related to next-day irritability in adolescent boys and may vary as a function of anger rumination and self-control. Additionally, irritability also showed a potential association with subsequent sleep. However, findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small, all-male adolescent sample. Future studies including larger and more diverse adolescent samples are needed to assess their generalizability and robustness.

papers.title: Electrophysiological Changes Before and After Glaucoma Filtration Surgery in the Mid-Postoperative Period: A Retrospective Study.
papers.abstract: Introduction Changes in retinal function during the first days after glaucoma filtration surgery have been documented with electroretinography (ERG), but little is known about later time points, particularly in eyes operated on without concurrent cataract surgery and in eyes that develop choroidal detachment (CD). We examined ERG parameters before and after filtration surgery performed alone and explored, as a hypothesis-generating analysis, whether the responses differed between eyes with and without postoperative CD. Methods Thirty-two eyes of 32 patients who underwent filtration surgery alone at Chiba University Hospital were reviewed retrospectively. Full-field ERGs were recorded with dilated pupils before surgery and 41.9 ± 18.3 days afterward using the RETeval system (LKC Technologies, Gaithersburg, MD), with the light-adapted 3.0 and dark-adapted 0.01 stimuli specified by the International Society for Clinical Electrophysiology of Vision (ISCEV) standard. Amplitudes and peak times of the photopic a- and b-waves and the scotopic b-wave were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and eyes were grouped according to the presence or absence of CD. Results Across the whole cohort, no amplitude or peak time changed significantly. In the CD group, the scotopic b-wave peak time shortened from 120.9 ± 12.0 ms to 114.6 ± 7.8 ms (p = 0.025), while the remaining parameters were unchanged; the non-CD group showed no significant change. Intraocular pressure (IOP) fell from 18.4 ± 4.4 to 8.3 ± 3.5 mmHg after surgery (p < 0.001). Conclusions Roughly six weeks after filtration surgery performed alone, ERG amplitudes were unchanged. This is compatible with a limited electrophysiological effect of surgery at this stage or with recovery from changes that occurred earlier, although the design does not allow the two to be distinguished. The shortening of the scotopic b-wave peak time in eyes with CD was an exploratory observation in eight eyes and requires confirmation in larger prospective studies.

papers.title: Quantifying Interictal Spike Asymmetry on Scalp EEG to Lateralize the Seizure-Onset Zone in Temporal Lobe Epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Accurate lateralization of the seizure focus in temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is critical for surgical planning. Our current approach of capturing multiple seizures often misses bilateral disease because of seizure-onset variability. Interictal spike rate asymmetry is a promising marker of TLE laterality. However, visual analysis has low interrater reliability and cannot estimate long-term spike rates. This study evaluated whether asymmetry of automatically detected interictal spikes on scalp EEG can lateralize the clinician-annotated seizure focus in TLE. We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients with drug-resistant TLE who underwent scalp EEG recording at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania. Spike rates were quantified using a validated deep learning model, with a novel leave-one-hemisphere-out approach developed to lateralize the side of the spikes. We developed a logistic regression model to predict the clinician-determined laterality. Model performance was assessed using the area under the ROC curve (AUC), accuracy, and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Of 365 included patients (205 women [56.2%]; median age 38, range 18-86 years), the training cohort comprised 261 patients and the independent, time-shifted validation cohort comprised 104. In the test cohort, classification of left TLE vs right/bilateral achieved an AUC of 0.78 (95% CI 0.69-0.87), an accuracy of 70%, and an AUPRC of 0.80 (95% CI 0.69-0.91), and classification of right TLE vs left/bilateral achieved an AUC of 0.80 (95% CI 0.70-0.88), an accuracy of 75%, and an AUPRC of 0.71 (95% CI 0.56-0.85). Model-surgery concordance was positively associated with favorable surgical outcomes. Engel I outcomes were associated with higher concordance probabilities (median difference = 0.20; 95% CI -0.02 to 0.39; r = 0.35; p = 0.037), and no significant association was observed for ILAE 1-2 (median difference = 0.20; 95% CI -0.06 to 0.38; r = 0.29; p = 0.084). Interictal spike asymmetry on scalp EEG shows promise as a noninvasive lateralizing marker in TLE. Applying this model could confirm TLE laterality when it agrees with other noninvasive data or identify patients with a high likelihood of bilateral TLE, potentially avoiding un-necessary invasive studies and reducing the number of seizures needed for evaluation.

papers.title: E-MDD: an evidence-guided explainable framework for EEG-based depression recognition.
papers.abstract: An evidence-guided explainable framework, E-MDD, is developed to integrate high-dimensional EEG representations, neurophysiological biomarkers, and large language models for the recognition of EEG-based depression with concise and evidence-based textual explanations. The proposed E-MDD framework consists of three stages: classification, evidence construction, and evidence-guided inference. In the classification stage, two parallel feature extraction branches are employed to extract Electroencephalography latent features and neurophysiological biomarkers, which are subsequently fused and fed into a lightweight multilayer perceptron for the recognition of depression. In the evidence construction stage, the latent feature dimensions of the EEG are aligned with neurophysiological biomarkers, and the model's decision basis is identified to construct structured evidence supporting the classification results. In the evidence-guided inference stage, structured evidence and the proposed evidence-guided prompt are used to guide the large language model in generating concise textual explanations. The experimental results on the Mumtaz dataset show that E-MDD achieves an AUC of 0.8472 and an F1-score of 0.8421. Meanwhile, the generated short-text explanations can effectively describe the basis of the model's decision-making for its predictions, demonstrating a high degree of faithfulness. The proposed framework also demonstrates consistent evidence-guided explanation performance across EEGNet and EEGConformer. Overall, this study proposes a neurophysiologically interpretable framework for EEG-based deep learning models, which effectively enhances the interpretability of deep learning models for depression detection and provides a new perspective for understanding their decision-making mechanisms.

papers.title: Electrophysiology Team-Administered Conscious Sedation for Pulsed-Field Versus Radiofrequency Ablation in Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.abstract: Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) is emerging as a novel nonthermal alternative. However, PFA is commonly performed under general anesthesia or deep sedation requiring anesthesiologists, which increases resource utilization and limits its widespread application. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of conscious sedation for PFA administered by the electrophysiology (EP) team, using radiofrequency ablation (RFA) as a comparator. A total of 120 patients with symptomatic, drug-refractory atrial fibrillation were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the PFA group or the RFA group. We evaluated three key outcomes: (1) intraoperative patient tolerance, assessed using validated scales (Faces Pain Scale-Revised [FPS-R], Likert Scale Questionnaire [LSQ]) combined with intraoperative body movement and cough reactions; (2) procedural efficiency; and (3) procedural safety. The incidence of pain during pulmonary vein isolation was comparable between the two groups (all p > 0.05), whereas FPS-R scores were significantly lower in the PFA group (p < 0.05). No significant difference was observed in movement scores between the two groups (p = 0.452). According to the LSQ analysis, only 1 patient (1.7%) in the RFA group reported dissatisfaction with intraoperative pain management. Cough incidence during PVI was higher with PFA (21.7% [13/60] vs 6.7% [4/60]; p = 0.018). Both total procedure time and left atrial dwell time were shorter in the PFA group. Furthermore, no serious complications were directly related to conscious sedation. In selected low-risk patients, EP team-administered conscious sedation is feasible for PFA, with acceptable intraoperative tolerance and safety while preserving procedural efficiency.

papers.title: Direct randomized evidence for systemic targeted therapies in prurigo nodularis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Systemic targeted therapies are reshaping treatment for prurigo nodularis (PN), but the timing of clinically meaningful benefits and the strength of supporting evidence remain unclear. We synthesized direct placebo-controlled evidence by outcome and follow-up time, distinguishing replicated phase 3 evidence from preliminary signals. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to June 30, 2026, for randomized controlled trials of systemic targeted therapies for PN. Compatible outcomes were pooled separately at prespecified time points using random-effects models. The primary outcome was a ≥ 4-point reduction in weekly average Worst Itch or Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale scores. Secondary outcomes included Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) success, dual response, sleep, quality of life, psychological outcomes, and safety. Risk of bias and certainty were assessed using RoB 2 and GRADE. Eleven trials involving 1,623 participants evaluated six therapies. Itch response favored active treatment at weeks 4 (RR 4.76, 95% CI 3.01-7.55), 12 (2.67, 1.43-5.00), 16 (3.32, 2.57-4.29), and 24 (3.09, 2.18-4.38), whereas the week 8 estimate was imprecise (1.73, 0.94-3.21). IGA success was supported from week 8 onward. Nemolizumab improved sleep response by week 4, and two phase 3 dupilumab trials showed a week 24 dual-response benefit (RR 3.98, 2.31-6.85). Treatment-emergent adverse events were modestly more frequent with active treatment (RR 1.14, 1.06-1.24), while serious adverse events and discontinuations did not clearly increase. The most robust evidence came from replicated phase 3 programs of dupilumab and nemolizumab. Replicated randomized evidence supports clinically meaningful improvements in itch and lesion outcomes with dupilumab and nemolizumab. Symptomatic benefits may emerge earlier than lesion responses, but this pattern should be interpreted cautiously because evidence across time points derives from limited, partly non-overlapping trial sets. Comparative treatment ranking is not supported, and longer-term data are needed to define rare, delayed, and agent-specific harms. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420261445753, identifier CRD420261445753.

papers.title: Serum magnesium levels and the risk of acute viral cardiomyopathy in children: A case-control study.
papers.abstract: Acute viral cardiomyopathy is a leading cause of heart failure in children. Although magnesium is essential for myocardial electrophysiology, its potential association with pediatric viral cardiomyopathy remains poorly characterized. This hospital-based frequency-matched case-control study (1:1 ratio, balanced for age) included 73 children with confirmed acute viral cardiomyopathy and 73 non-cardiac hospitalized controls at Afzalipour Hospital, Kerman, Iran (2023-2024). Serum total magnesium was measured on admission (reference 1.7-2.3 mg/dL); hypomagnesemia was defined as <1.7 mg/dL. Groups were compared using an independent-samples t-test and a χ² test. Multivariable logistic regression has been used to assess associated factors for acute viral cardiomyopathy. Mean serum magnesium level was significantly lower in the cardiomyopathy group than the control group (1.80 ± 0.31 vs. 1.98 ± 0.31 mg/dL; P = 0.003). Hypomagnesemia prevalence was significantly higher in the cardiomyopathy group (39.7% vs. 9.6%; unadjusted OR (95% CI): 5.80 (2.28-14.75); P < 0.001). After adjustment for sex, BMI, fever, and underlying chronic disease, each 0.1 mg/dL decrease in serum magnesium was associated with 1.38-fold higher odds of cardiomyopathy (adjusted OR (95% CI): 1.38 (1.11-1.72); P = 0.004). Hospital stay was longer in cases (7.77 ± 2.42 vs. 5.39 ± 2.20 days; P < 0.001). In-hospital mortality was higher among the cardiomyopathy group (6.8% vs. 1.4%), though the difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.209). Children with acute viral cardiomyopathy seem to have significantly lower serum magnesium compared with matched controls. Routine admission magnesium screening could be considered in management protocols.
keywords: Acute Viral Cardiomyopathy; Hypomagnesemia; Magnesium; Pediatrics; Cardiology

papers.title: Naturalistic language assessment and brain-network biomarkers in post-stroke aphasia for precision neurorehabilitation.
papers.abstract: Advances in naturalistic language assessment, portable neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and brain-network modeling are creating new opportunities to evaluate post-stroke aphasia under conditions closer to real-world communication. Conventional aphasia batteries and isolated linguistic tasks remain essential for diagnosis, severity classification, and treatment planning, but they provide limited information about how language-network activity supports communication in dynamic, naturalistic contexts. This integrative review, informed by a structured literature search and descriptive thematic mapping, synthesizes evidence on connected speech, discourse production, narrative comprehension, interactive communication, and contextual reading after stroke. We examine how multilevel features from these behaviors can be organized into graded, interacting dimensions of lexical-semantic access, phonological encoding, grammatical organization, discourse processing, executive-predictive control, and speech-motor output. We further review multimodal evidence from fNIRS, fMRI, EEG/ERP, lesion-symptom mapping, structural connectivity, and functional connectivity, highlighting residual left-hemisphere language networks, conditional right-hemisphere support, bilateral reorganization, domain-general control systems, and longitudinal recovery. Portable EEG and fNIRS are considered complementary approaches for repeated assessment during less constrained language tasks, with distinct temporal, spatial, and practical trade-offs. Building on this evidence, we propose an operational ecological biomarker framework that links task choice, multilevel feature extraction, multivariate behavioral profiles, neural measures, prespecified clinical questions, and longitudinal outcomes. This framework may support recovery prediction, rehabilitation stratification, neuromodulation target selection, individualized therapy planning, and monitoring of functional communication.

papers.title: Circadian-melatonin signaling in general anesthesia: molecular mechanisms and perioperative implications.
papers.abstract: Anesthesia and surgery are delivered to a temporally organized organism whose physiology is governed by the suprachiasmatic nucleus, peripheral molecular clocks, and pineal melatonin signaling. This review synthesizes mechanistic, preclinical, and clinical evidence on how anesthetic agents, surgical stress, and the perioperative environment interact with circadian and melatonergic signaling, and on whether that interaction can be targeted therapeutically. In rodent and cellular studies, volatile and intravenous anesthetics alter clock function in an agent- and phase-dependent manner; proposed mechanisms include GABAergic and glutamatergic modulation of entrainment, transcriptional and chromatin-level repression of CLOCK-BMAL1/PER-CRY signaling, and metabolic coupling through CaMK-CREB, AMPK, SIRT1, and GSK-3β. These mechanisms have not been confirmed in humans. In patients, these effects are inseparable from surgical injury, opioids, fasting, inflammation, and disrupted light-dark exposure, all of which suppress melatonin amplitude, delay its onset, and promote internal desynchrony. Melatonin signals through MT1 and MT2 receptors to produce chronobiotic, anxiolytic, and antinociceptive effects, whereas the mitochondrial, redox, and anti-inflammatory actions, described almost exclusively in animal and cellular models, require substantially higher exposures and have not been demonstrated in surgical patients; the two arms are pharmacologically distinct and should not be pooled. Clinically, preoperative anxiolysis with melatonin in adults is the most consistently supported indication, whereas evidence for postoperative sleep, analgesia, delirium prevention, and organ protection remains heterogeneous and of low certainty. Most trials have used fixed clock-time dosing without measuring internal circadian phase or achieved plasma exposure, so null results cannot distinguish an ineffective mechanism from an inadequate intervention. The circadian-melatonin axis remains a plausible perioperative target, but clinical translation requires phase-aware, exposure-informed, and adequately powered trials.

papers.title: Long-Term Outcome of West Syndrome Treated With Adrenocorticotropic Hormone-Based Therapy in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Bangladesh.
papers.abstract: Background West syndrome is a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy associated with epileptic spasms, abnormal EEG findings, and poor long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes. Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-based therapies are widely used for treatment, but data on seizure, EEG, and developmental outcomes from Bangladesh remain limited. Objective The aim of this study was to evaluate seizure outcomes, EEG changes, and long-term functional developmental outcomes among children with West syndrome treated with different ACTH-based regimens in a tertiary care hospital in Bangladesh. Methods This retrospective observational follow-up study included 50 children with West syndrome treated at the Department of Pediatric Neurology, National Institute of Neurosciences & Hospital, Dhaka, Bangladesh, between 2018 and 2024. Children were categorized into three treatment groups: high-dose ACTH, n = 18; combination therapy with high-dose ACTH plus vigabatrin, n = 10; and medium-dose ACTH, n = 22. Seizure outcomes, post-treatment EEG findings, and long-term functional developmental outcomes were assessed from clinical records, EEG reports, caregiver interviews, and structured parental surveys. Data were analyzed using SPSS Version 22.0, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Results Baseline age distribution, age at onset of spasms, and sex did not differ significantly among treatment groups. Seizure outcome differed significantly across groups, with seizure freedom observed in 61.1% of children in the high-dose ACTH group, 50.0% in the combination therapy group, and 4.5% in the medium-dose ACTH group. Lennox-Gastaut syndrome was most frequent in the medium-dose ACTH group, 72.7%. EEG normalization was highest in the high-dose ACTH group, 44.4%, followed by the combination therapy group, 20.0%, and the medium-dose ACTH group, 13.6%, although this difference was not statistically significant. Developmental outcome also did not differ significantly among groups; however, dependent living was most frequent in the medium-dose ACTH group, 59.1%. Conclusion High-dose ACTH was associated with better seizure freedom and a higher proportion of EEG normalization in this cohort, while medium-dose ACTH was associated with poorer seizure outcome, more frequent Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, and greater developmental dependency. However, the retrospective non-randomized design and small sample size limit causal interpretation. Larger prospective studies with standardized treatment protocols, etiological classification, relapse assessment, adverse-effect monitoring, and validated developmental evaluation are needed.

papers.title: A mixed-methods study of depressive-symptom severity among Thai university students and the underestimated role of social media.
papers.abstract: University students face academic, social, economic, and digital stressors. Social-media use may be under-recognized as a correlate of depressive symptoms because online engagement is often viewed as routine communication, leisure, and academic activity. This study examined factors associated with depressive-symptom severity among Thai university students and explored the mismatch between perceived stressors and the observed association with social-media use. A cross-sectional mixed-methods study was conducted among 789 undergraduates at Rangsit University, Thailand. Quantitative data were collected using a structured questionnaire and the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D), categorized as low symptoms (0-15), mild-to-moderate (16-26), or severe (27-60) symptoms. Associations were examined using χ 2 tests and ordinal logistic regression. A purposive subsample of 12 students participated in semi-structured interviews on social-media routines, online comparison, nighttime use and sleep, coping, social support, and help-seeking. All interviews were audio-recorded and supplemented by contemporaneous field notes. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically and integrated with quantitative findings through joint comparison. Clinically significant depressive symptoms (CES-D ≥ 16) were reported by 49.68% of students. Academic year, major, GPAX, primary source of personal support, and daily social-media use were independently associated with symptom severity. Compared with students using social media >3 h/day, those using it <1 h/day (OR = 0.125, 95% CI: 0.040-0.391) or 1-3 h/day (OR = 0.424, 95% CI: 0.278-0.647) had lower odds of greater symptom severity. Internet/social-media use ranked only fifth among eight perceived stressors (37.01% agreement). Three qualitative themes described social media as an embedded and ambivalent part of student life, psychological effects shaped by patterns and interpretations of use, and distress managed mainly through self-coping and trusted informal support. The key mixed-methods finding was a perception-association mismatch: social-media use was not perceived as a leading stressor yet showed the strongest adjusted association with depressive-symptom severity among the factors examined. These cross-sectional findings do not establish causality but support digital-wellbeing assessment beyond duration alone.
papers.journal: Frontiers in child and adolescent psychiatry

papers.title: Sleep disturbance is associated with reduced DTI-ALPS index and altered functional-network efficiency in internet gaming disorder.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance is common in internet gaming disorder (IGD), but its possible involvement in the pathophysiology of IGD remains unclear. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the glymphatic system-related function in IGD patients and to establish the associations among glymphatic system, human brain network, and clinical features. This study recruited 66 IGD patients and 35 healthy controls (HC), who underwent magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanning and clinical assessment. The glymphatic system-related diffusivity and network efficiency were calculated based on diffusion images along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) method and resting-state functional MRI, respectively. Differences between groups, neural/clinical correlations, and mediation analyses were further explored. Compared with HC, IGD patients showed a significantly lower ALPS index and global network efficiency. The partial correlation analysis showed that the ALPS index in IGD patients was associated with PSQI, HAMA, and HAMD scores. Moreover, the ALPS index partially mediated the association between global brain efficiency and sleep quality in exploratory cross-sectional mediation analysis. The current study revealed abnormalities of ALPS index and network efficiency in IGD patients and suggested that the cross-sectional associations among global brain efficiency, sleep quality, and ALPS index were consistent with an indirect pathway, which may reveal the neuropathological mechanisms of IGD.
keywords: diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular space

papers.title: Functional brain activity in cancer-related cognitive impairment: a scoping review of EEG studies.
papers.abstract: Cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI) is reported across the cancer trajectory, yet its neurobiological basis remains incompletely understood. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a temporally precise method for assessing brain activity at rest and during cognitive processing, but its application in CRCI research has not been systematically mapped. This scoping review characterized how EEG has been used to study cognitive functioning in people with cancer, including populations studied, EEG paradigms and analytic approaches employed, and cognitive outcomes assessed. Following PRISMA-ScR guidance, we searched MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Web of Science from inception to February 2025 for studies using EEG to examine cognitive functioning. Sixty articles were included. Most were small and cross-sectional, with publication output increasing markedly after 2015. Task-based event-related potentials, particularly from oddball and attention tasks, were used most frequently, whereas quantitative EEG approaches, including spectral power and connectivity analyses, were less common. In populations with cancers outside the central nervous system (CNS), longer P300 latency and lower amplitude were common, but opposite and null findings also occurred. Evidence from primary CNS and other intracranial tumor populations was sparse. Across cancer contexts, quantitative EEG findings showed limited convergence across articles. Associations between EEG measures and cognitive outcomes were inconsistent and often not tested directly. Overall, EEG provides a complementary approach to investigating cognition in people with cancer, but the evidence remains methodologically heterogeneous. Larger longitudinal studies, more consistent cognitive outcome selection, and closer integration of neural and cognitive measures are needed to establish reproducible findings and evaluate their potential clinical utility. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251084951.

papers.title: The health-promoting functions of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and lactic acid bacteria metabolism: From biosynthesis to applications in the food industry.
papers.abstract: GABA is a principal inhibitory neurotransmitter with systemic regulatory roles. This review synthesizes the health-promoting functions of GABA and the molecular mechanisms of its production in LAB. GABA regulates neuronal excitability via GABA receptors, suppresses inflammation by inhibiting the TLR4/NF-κB pathway, and modulates the gut-brain axis through microbiota remodeling. LAB synthesize GABA primarily via the glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD) system, with an alternative GABA-T-mediated non-GAD pathway that requires further validation, a process tightly coupled to acid resistance. Optimization strategies include genetic engineering, fermentation control, physical stimulation, and synthetic co-culture. These strains are widely applied in dairy, plant-based beverages, and meat, enhancing flavor while sleep-improving, and microbiota-modulating benefits. However, significant challenges persist, including incomplete substrate conversion causing off-flavors, poor GABA stability in food, and genetic instability during scale-up. This work uniquely integrates non-neuronal GABA functions, metabolic diversity beyond the canonical GAD pathway, and practical challenges of GABA incorporation into food matrices.

papers.title: Remimazolam for Procedural Sedation During Synchronized Electrical Cardioversion in the Emergency Department.
papers.abstract: Synchronized electrical cardioversion necessitates procedural sedation to ensure patient comfort and amnesia. Remimazolam is a novel, ultrashort-acting intravenous benzodiazepine with organ-independent esterase metabolism, a favorable safety profile, and flumazenil reversibility. Although, previously described in the electrophysiology laboratory, use of remimazolam has not been reported for electrical cardioversion in the emergency department. In this case, a 67-year-old man with sudden-onset paroxysmal atrial fibrillation presented in symptomatic atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Following rate and rhythm optimization, the decision was made to proceed with synchronized electrical cardioversion under procedural sedation. After consent was obtained, remimazolam (5 mg intravenously) was administered as a single bolus. Sedation onset occurred at 49 seconds, with adequate depth achieved at 1 minute 37 seconds. A single synchronized biphasic 200 joule electric shock was successfully delivered at 2 minutes 20 seconds, converting the patient to normal sinus rhythm. Eye opening occurred at 3 minutes 50 seconds, with return to baseline orientation at 4 minutes 30 seconds. No apnea, hypoxia, hemodynamic instability, or procedural recall was observed. Continuous end-tidal carbon dioxide monitoring confirmed uninterrupted spontaneous ventilation throughout. The rapid onset, hemodynamic stability, and remarkably brief recovery time observed support its potential as a first-line sedative for emergency department cardioversion. Further prospective study in this setting is warranted.
papers.journal: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

papers.title: Magnetocardiographic characteristics in patients with varying severity of obstructive sleep apnea syndrome.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS) is an established risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Magnetocardiography (MCG) is an emerging non-invasive electrophysiological technique with potential value in cardiovascular assessment; however, its utility in evaluating OSAS severity remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize MCG features across different severities of OSAS and to evaluate their predictive performance for moderate-to-severe disease. This retrospective study enrolled OSAS patients between June 2023 and October 2024, all of whom underwent MCG examination. Patients were stratified by OSAS severity, and MCG parameters were compared between the normal-to-mild and moderate-to-severe groups. Baseline data, complete blood count, serum biochemical indicators, and MCG parameters were collected along with relevant clinical and laboratory data. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of moderate-to-severe OSAS, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed to evaluate the predictive performance of each parameter and the combined model. Group comparisons revealed significant differences in traditional OSAS severity risk factors (sex, body mass index, etc.). Diastolic function indicators, including E/A ratio and left atrial size, also showed marked differences between groups, with the moderate-to-severe subgroup exhibiting larger left atria and a higher proportion of E/A ratio values below 1. Univariate analysis identified 35 MCG parameters that differed between groups, while multivariate regression retained four independent predictors (htrt, tmdf, RS-didma, and qr_rela_dist_neg_mode). ROC analysis indicated that T-wave- and QRS-wave-related indices had moderate predictive value; a combined model incorporating htrt, tmdf, and RS-didma showed superior area under the curve compared to any single parameter. MCG parameters demonstrate distinct characteristics across OSAS severity levels and yield favorable predictive performance for moderate-to-severe OSAS, positioning MCG as a promising non-invasive tool for early diagnosis. The observed changes in diastolic function markers may suggest underlying coronary microcirculatory alterations in patients with moderate-to-severe OSAS. Rigorously designed prospective studies are warranted to validate MCG as a standardized diagnostic modality for OSAS-related coronary microcirculation disorder.

papers.title: Case Report: Smith-Magenis syndrome with bilateral high-grade vesicoureteral reflux, hypothyroidism, and seizure in infancy.
papers.abstract: Smith-Magenis syndrome (SMS) is a rare neurodevelopmental and multisystem disorder caused mainly by 17p11.2 deletions involving RAI1. Because the characteristic behavioral and sleep phenotype may not yet be apparent, diagnosis in infancy can be challenging. We report a 9-month-old boy with recurrent febrile urinary tract infection, bilateral hydronephrosis with ureteral dilatation, hypothyroidism, global developmental delay, hypotonia, brachydactyly, dysmorphic features, phimosis, and short penis. Voiding cystourethrography demonstrated bilateral grade IV vesicoureteral reflux (VUR). Renal scintigraphy showed focal right renal cortical defects; DTPA effective renal plasma flow was 180.33 mL/min in the left kidney and 133.77 mL/min in the right kidney, corresponding to split function of 57.4% and 42.6%. Trio whole-exome sequencing with copy-number-variant analysis identified a de novo 3.63-Mb deletion at 17p11.2 encompassing RAI1, confirming SMS; a maternally inherited heterozygous DUOX2 likely pathogenic variant was also detected, but its contribution to hypothyroidism remains unproven. Infection improved with antibiotics, levothyroxine was resumed, and amoxicillin/clavulanate prophylaxis was initiated. Surgery for phimosis was postponed after an afebrile sleep-related seizure. Follow-up showed improved renal indices, no recurrent urinary tract infection, normalized thyroid function, and no definite abnormality on video-electroencephalography, although developmental delay persisted and brief seizure-like ocular events remained under evaluation. This case shows that high-grade bilateral VUR with recurrent infection and a syndromic neurodevelopmental phenotype can be an early presentation of SMS and warrants copy-number analysis, renal protection, and coordinated endocrine, neurologic, developmental, and urologic follow-up.

papers.title: Dynamic adaptation of attentional control across bilingual interactional contexts.
papers.abstract: Bilingual experience is thought to shape cognitive control via adaptive attentional reorganization, yet the neural mechanisms by which different interactional contexts dynamically modulate attentional control remain unclear. This study used EEG to examine how Chinese monolingual, English monolingual, bilingual, and voluntary naming contexts influence attentional control in Chinese-English bilinguals. Thirty-five bilinguals completed picture-naming tasks in different contexts, followed by an antisaccade task with concurrent EEG. We analyzed reaction time, ERPs, frontal and parietal delta/theta power, and frontoparietal functional connectivity (wPLI). Bilingual and voluntary naming contexts shortened antisaccade reaction times (all p < 0.01). No significant main effect of context was found on N2 amplitudes (p = 0.615). Both contexts reduced parietal delta and theta power relative to the English monolingual context (all p < 0.05). Exploratory connectivity analysis initially suggested bilingual-context effects, but this finding did not survive homologous ROI validation. These preliminary sensor-level findings await validation by source-localized EEG or fMRI. These findings suggest that bilingual and voluntary naming contexts may facilitate attentional control through adaptive reorganization of the attentional system rather than through enhancing a specific inhibitory process. This pattern is consistent with the adaptationist perspective on bilingual cognition and provides preliminary neural evidence for the language mode theory.

papers.title: Association of the metabolic signature of sleep patterns with breast cancer risk: a prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Existing evidence regarding the association between sleep patterns and breast cancer development remains inconsistent. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between sleep patterns and breast cancer risk while examining the potential mediating effects of sleep score-related metabolic signatures. A total of 220,089 participants from the UK Biobank study were analyzed. Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine the relationships among the sleep score (based on 5 sleep factors), genetic risk (based on 22 variants), metabolic signature (derived from 251 metabolites), and breast cancer incidence, adjusting for age, BMI, sociodemographic, and lifestyle factors. Mediation analysis was used to test whether the metabolic signature mediated the association between the sleep score and breast cancer risk. A total of 8459 incident breast cancer cases (3.84% of the cohort) were identified during a median follow-up of 11.6 years. Compared with individuals with a sleep score of 5 points, those with a score of 0-1 points had a significantly greater risk of developing breast cancer (HR = 1.30, 95% CI = 1.11-1.52). The sleep-related metabolic signature was also associated with elevated breast cancer risk (HR = 1.62, 95% CI = 1.32-1.99). Mediation analysis revealed that the metabolic signature accounted for 13.5% of the observed association between the sleep score and the incidence of breast cancer. Maintaining healthy sleep patterns may lower the risk of breast cancer irrespective of genetic predispositions. The metabolic signature partially mediated the association between the sleep score and breast cancer development.

papers.title: Improved Upper-Airway Collapse Imaging in Obstructive Sleep Apnea Using Self-Supervised Spiral Variational Manifold Learning.
papers.abstract: To propose a self-supervised variational manifold learning framework for dynamic upper-airway MRI reconstruction in obstructive sleep apnea from prospectively under-sampled spiral data during natural sleep, without requiring fully sampled training data. A CNN generator and low-dimensional latent vectors were jointly optimized directly from prospectively under-sampled spiral k-space measurements, learning a subject-specific temporal manifold without an explicit motion model. A validation loss guided adaptive learning rate provided principled early stopping without ground truth. Eleven concurrent axial slices from velo-pharynx to hypo-pharynx were reconstructed at 183 ms temporal resolution and 11 × acceleration across 8 OSA patients during natural sleep and 4 healthy volunteers performing the Müller maneuver. Reconstruction quality was compared against parallel imaging, compressed sensing, view sharing, and analysis-manifold reconstruction. Three expert raters independently assessed image quality using a four-point ordinal rubric. The proposed method resolved multi-site airway collapse across 11 contiguous slices, including simultaneous visualization of complete concentric retro-palatal collapse, lateral collapse at the velo-pharyngeal to oro-pharyngeal transition, and partial tongue-base and oropharyngeal narrowing. Expert scores were superior across aliasing, spatial blurring, and temporal blurring categories ( p < 0.001 , pairwise Mann-Whitney U tests). Reconstructed airway dynamics were corroborated by concurrent respiratory effort and SpO 2 signals, with up to 13 obstructive events identified within a single imaging run. Reconstruction artifacts occurred in 8 of 132 slices (6%) and did not compromise airway visualization. Self-supervised variational manifold learning demonstrates the feasibility of robust dynamic upper-airway MRI during natural sleep, with potential to inform future OSA phenotyping and surgical-planning studies.

papers.title: [Sleep apnea in older adults: should it always be treated?].
papers.abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) affects more than 50 % of people over 65 years but often remains underdiagnosed due to atypical presentation: classic symptoms (snoring, daytime sleepiness) are less pronounced, while insomnia is more frequent.
