papers.title: Prevalence of Suspected Obstructive Sleep Apnea Among Patients With Chronic Cough and Relatively Low BMI.
papers.abstract: Recent studies have suggested an association between chronic cough and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of suspected OSA and describe associated clinical characteristics among Japanese adults with chronic cough. Outpatients with chronic cough were recruited from three Japanese institutions between March 2023 and February 2025. Eligible participants were ≥20 years old with a cough lasting >8 weeks. Overnight home sleep apnea testing was performed to assess the respiratory event index (REI), and suspected OSA was defined as an REI ≥5 events/h. Cough-related symptoms were assessed using the visual analog scale (VAS) and the Japanese version of the Leicester Cough Questionnaire (J-LCQ), and daytime sleepiness was evaluated using the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS). REI was compared across causes of chronic cough. Patients were stratified by REI ≥15 events/h. Correlations between the REI and age, body mass index (BMI), VAS score, and J-LCQ score were evaluated. This study enrolled 23 patients (median age, 56.0 years; 11 men). The median BMI was 25.2 kg/m2. Suspected OSA was present in 20 patients (87.0%), despite a median ESS score of 7.0. The median REI was 15.6 events/h and was elevated regardless of the cause of chronic cough. REI ≥ 15 events/h was associated with older age (p=0.04), whereas BMI did not differ significantly between the groups. J-LCQ scores were not significantly associated with the REI. REI was high in patients with chronic cough, suggesting a high prevalence of suspected OSA despite their relatively low BMI. These findings suggest obesity-independent mechanisms and support OSA screening even in patients without daytime sleepiness.

papers.title: Improved motor learning in adenosine A1 receptor knockout mice.
papers.abstract: Adenosine is a widespread neuromodulator, acting at A1 and A2A receptors in the brain. Adenosine plays role in a multitude of functions including sleep, homeostasis, neuroprotection and synaptic plasticity. Deletion of A1Rs in knock-out mice (A1R KO) revealed non-uniform effects on learning: learning sequential visual discrimination tasks was impaired, while spatial learning (Morris maze) and working memory tasks were not. Motor learning was also preserved in A1R KO mice. However, a systematic comparison of motor learning in KO and wild type (WT) mice has not been performed. Here we fill this knowledge gap by comparing motor learning in WT and A1R KO mice using an accelerating rotarod task. Both genotypes acquired motor skill and retained it after 1 week without further training. Genotype and Age had significant effects on improvement of motor skills relative to initial performance. A1R KO mice showed higher rate of learning than WT across training days, and reached better performance by the end of training (Day 5). However, retention after 1 week was better in WT mice, which improved relative to last day of training, while KO animals performed at the same level. We saw no differences between females and males, but older animals showed greater gains during learning and better retention. Finally, individual variability of motor learning was not related to measures of baseline motor activity, or anxiety. These results add new pieces to a multifaceted and intriguing picture of shifts in the brain functions resulting from A1R loss and warrant further exploration.

papers.title: Effects of Probiotic Supplementation on Depression, Anxiety, and Sleep Quality in Healthy Participants: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of probiotic supplementation on depression, anxiety, and sleep quality in healthy adults. PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Embase were searched from inception to September 18, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing probiotics with placebo for ≥4 weeks were included. Data from 20 studies involving 1,508 participants were analyzed using Stata 17.0. Random-effects or fixed-effects models were selected according to heterogeneity. The GRADE approach was used to assess evidence certainty. Probiotics significantly reduced depression scores (SMD = -0.23, 95% CI: -0.36 to -0.10, P < 0.01; I² = 4.67%) and improved sleep quality (SMD = -0.37, 95% CI: -0.52 to -0.22, P < 0.01; I² = 41.67%). However, the overall effect on anxiety was not significant (SMD = -0.11, 95% CI: -0.31 to 0.09, P = 0.27; I² = 61.41%). Subgroup analyses were exploratory and unadjusted; no definitive conclusion can be drawn regarding intervention duration or strain type. GRADE certainty was moderate for depression and sleep quality, but very low for anxiety. In conclusion, probiotic supplementation may alleviate depressive symptoms and improve sleep quality in healthy adults, whereas its effect on anxiety remains inconclusive. Larger, standardized RCTs are needed to confirm these findings and clarify strain-specific effects.

papers.title: Over a billion more dark-morning school commutes for K-12 children under the Sunshine Protection Act.
papers.abstract: The US House's approval of the Sunshine Protection Act has revived the debate between permanent daylight saving time (DST) and standard time (ST). Permanent DST would push school start times before sunrise in many regions. Health, sleep, and scientific organizations favor permanent ST because it keeps solar, biological, and social time better aligned,1 which matters most for children and adolescents, whose rigid school schedules already conflict with their biological night and are linked to poor sleep and reduced cognitive and academic performance.2,3,4 The safety consequences of the proposed change remain unquantified, but for children, morning light availability matters most, since most return home in daylight regardless of clock policy. Using real school start times for 14 states that have approved permanent DST5 and local sunrise times, we counted pre-sunrise commutes to school under each clock regime. Across the 14 states analyzed, permanent DST would require pre-sunrise departures for most of the winter, adding approximately 356 million days of pre-sunrise travel events among school-aged children (child days) relative to the current system (seasonally alternating between ST and DST). Applying the same approach nationwide, permanent DST would add more than 2 billion dark-morning commutes yearly. Analyzing a decade of national fatal crash records, we found higher odds of pedestrian involvement in dark-morning crashes than light-morning ones (odds ratio [OR] 1.77) and among pedestrians aged 5-18 (OR 2.22). Permanent DST would expose many more children to elevated pedestrian-crash risk, evidence that is relevant to the US' choice of a time standard.

papers.title: Investigation of sleep patterns in pediatric liver transplant patients.
papers.abstract: This study was conducted to evaluate the sleep patterns of pediatric patients who had undergone liver transplants. This descriptive study involving 60 children was conducted between April and August 2025 at the Liver Transplantation Clinic of İnönü University. The research data were collected using demographic and clinical information forms and actigraph devices. Half of the children were girls, 38.3% were aged 7-12years, and 43.3% had undergone organ transplantation within the first 6months after transplantation. A sleep assessment revealed that the children slept for an average of 6.25±2.25h per day, achieved a sleep efficiency of 74.6±13.2%, experienced an average of 62.5±39.2min of wakefulness during sleep, and awoke an average of 40.4±19.6 times per night. Furthermore, a negative correlation was found between children's age and both the duration of awakenings (r=-0.322, p=0.012) and the number of awakenings (r=-0.279, p=0.031) during sleep. It was also found that children who complained of itching had significantly shorter sleep durations (U=99.000, Z=-2.370, p=0.018). This study shows that children who have undergone liver transplantation generally sleep for shorter periods and that this is more pronounced in those who experience itching. Nurses should routinely assess sleep in pediatric liver transplant recipients and implement personalized sleep hygiene interventions. Particular attention should be given to managing pruritus to improve sleep and recovery outcomes.

papers.title: Machine learning based on behavioral, fecal and oocyst analyses for chicken coccidiosis diagnosis: A systematic review with exploratory extension.
papers.abstract: In the context of large-scale and intensive poultry farming, avian coccidiosis causes substantial economic losses. Timely and accurate diagnosis is essential for effective control and prevention. However, conventional diagnostic methods, including microscopic examination and molecular assays, are constrained by limited efficiency and a heavy reliance on specialized expertise, rendering them inadequate for real-time, high-throughput diagnosis in modern farming systems. Recent advances in machine learning have demonstrated significant potential in image recognition and early disease detection, particularly for diagnosing coccidiosis based on fecal and oocyst images, positioning this technology as a promising tool for future diagnosis of avian coccidiosis. Despite considerable progress in this area, approaches that rely solely on fecal and oocyst recognition face challenges in early screening. Moreover, limitations in current datasets and models often lead to insufficient generalization under practical farming conditions. Furthermore, although monitoring behavioral and physiological abnormalities could facilitate early detection, research on this aspect remains largely unexplored for avian coccidiosis. To address these gaps, this systematic review with exploratory extension adopts a three-dimensional framework, "behavioral physiology, fecal characteristics, and oocyst morphology" to systematically summarize the current applications and challenges of machine learning in identifying avian coccidiosis, with the aim of clarifying existing research gaps and technical bottlenecks. Finally, to systematically meet the demand for early and efficient diagnosis, this review proposes a conceptual framework for an AI-based surveillance system for chicken coccidiosis that integrates multimodal data across behavioral screening, fecal validation, and oocyst-based analysis encompassing species identification, oocyst counting, sporulation-state classification and viability assessment. This framework will serve as a theoretical foundation for moving the field from laboratory research toward field applications, thereby enabling early, precise, efficient, and intelligent prevention and control of avian coccidiosis.

papers.title: Indoor NO2, temperature, and humidity in relation to maternal stress, sleep, and cognitive performance during pregnancy.
papers.abstract: Evidence characterising indoor environmental exposures and their effects on maternal neurobehavioural well-being during pregnancy remains scarce. To estimate the associations between indoor residential environmental exposures (nitrogen dioxide (NO2), temperature, and relative humidity (RH)) and maternal neurobehavioural well-being (measured as perceived stress, sleep quality, and cognitive performance). We included pregnant individuals (n = 906) from the population-based Barcelona Life Study Cohort (BiSC) who were recruited from 2018 to 2021. Weekly average indoor residential NO2 concentrations, temperature, and RH were objectively measured in participants' homes at ∼ 12 and ∼ 32 weeks of gestation using indoor monitoring devices. Linear, negative binomial, and mixed-effects regression models estimated the associations between indoor environmental exposures and perceived stress (10-item Perceived Stress Scale [PSS-10]), sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index [PSQI]), and cognitive performance (N-back reaction time and Primary Mental Abilities-Revised [PMA-R]); PSQI was assessed at both visits, while PSS-10 and cognitive tests were performed at ∼ 32 weeks of gestation only. After covariate adjustment, higher indoor NO2 exposure was associated with higher perceived stress (0.66 points (95 % confidence interval [CI] 0.11, 1.21; p = 0.019)) and a greater increase in PSS-10 scores for a NO2 interquartile range increase (11.2 µg/m3) but not with sleep quality or cognitive performance. Indoor temperature and RH metrics, including nighttime minima and maxima, were not associated with any outcome. Our findings suggest an association between indoor NO2 concentration and prenatal perceived stress, indicating that the residential environment may be a relevant factor in maternal antenatal health that warrants further investigation.

papers.title: Deep learning-assisted portable sensing platform based on a fluorescent MOF-polymer mixed-matrix membrane for rapid detection of nitrazepam in biological samples.
papers.abstract: Nitrazepam (NZP) is a benzodiazepine sedative-hypnotic widely used in the treatment of anxiety and sleep disorders. However, non-medical use of NZP as a new psychoactive substance poses serious health risks. Therefore, rapid and accurate detection of NZP in biological samples is important for point-of-care testing. Herein, a deep learning-assisted fluorescent sensing platform was developed based on a mixed-matrix membrane (1@PMMA), fabricated by incorporating a Cd-MOF, {[Cd(L)(H2O)2]·3H2O}n (1) (H2L = 5-(3-(pyridin-4-yl)ureido)isophthalic acid), into a poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) matrix for NZP detection. The resulting 1@PMMA exhibited good mechanical stability, processability, and fluorescence stability in biological samples. Upon exposure to NZP, 1@PMMA showed efficient fluorescence quenching, with a quenching efficiency of 96.19%, a detection limit of 0.21 μM, and a response time of approximately 2 s. The membrane maintained high selectivity in the presence of common biological components and stable sensing performance over five quenching-regeneration cycles. A smartphone-based fluorescence sensing method enabled portable visual detection of NZP through extraction of RGB values from fluorescence images of 1@PMMA. Additionally, a deep learning-based photo-to-result platform employing a ResNet-18 model directly predicted NZP concentrations from fluorescence images without manual data processing, showing a strong linear relationship between predicted and experimental concentrations (R2 = 0.9949). For spiked urine and serum samples, recoveries of 95.18-100.46% were obtained, with relative standard deviations of 0.18-3.10%. This work integrates a fluorescent MOF-based mixed-matrix membrane with a deep learning-assisted photo-to-result strategy for on-site quantitative determination of NZP in biological samples.

papers.title: Clinical outcomes and risk factors in pediatric epilepsy associated with focal cortical dysplasia: a retrospective cohort study of 628 imaging-confirmed cases.
papers.abstract: To investigate the clinical high-risk factors for epilepsy secondary to focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) in children and for progression to drug-resistant epilepsy, and to evaluate the long-term prognosis of affected patients. We retrospectively included 628 children with MRI-diagnosed FCD who were treated at the Children's Hospital of Chongqing Medical University between February 2006 and September 2025. Risk factors for epilepsy and drug-resistant epilepsy were analyzed using Cox and Logistic regression models, with cluster analysis applied to define clinical subtypes and the stability of the clustering solution was verified by bootstrap resampling. The incidence of epilepsy in children with FCD was 79.0% (496/628), of whom 24.0% (151/628) progressed to drug-resistant epilepsy. Among the 81 surgically treated children with medium- to long-term follow-up, 72.8% (59/81) achieved complete seizure freedom. Multivariate Cox regression analysis demonstrated that global developmental delay (P=0.004), intellectual disability (P=0.002), paralysis (P=0.014), hypoplasia of the white matter (P<0.001), repetitive epileptiform discharges lasting ≥5 seconds during the interictal period (P=0.003), and continuous irregular slow waves (P=0.016) were independently associated with epilepsy onset. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis showed that the interictal RED type II waveform (P=0.003) was an independent high-risk factor for drug-resistant epilepsy. Cluster analysis classified the patients into three subtypes: a low-risk group characterized by seizure freedom or drug responsiveness, essentially normal intelligence, lesions confined to a single lobe, and no EEG abnormalities; an intermediate-risk group, also predominantly seizure-free or drug-responsive, but frequently accompanied by intellectual disability, with single-lobe lesions and a single abnormal EEG pattern; and a high-risk group dominated by drug-resistant epilepsy, often complicated by intellectual disability, with lesions frequently involving multiple lobes and multiple abnormal EEG patterns. Bootstrap validation indicated moderate stability of the clustering structure (ARI = 0.653). Children with FCD show marked clinical heterogeneity, and their prognosis is closely associated with neurodevelopmental deficits, lesion extent, and electrophysiological characteristics. Early identification of these high-risk factors, together with cluster-based stratified management, may be of substantial importance for improving patient outcomes.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnoea is associated with reduced semen quality and compartmentalized seminal inflammation: A prospective cohort with non-randomized CPAP follow-up.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is associated with systemic inflammation and male reproductive dysfunction, but its relationship with semen quality and local seminal inflammation remains unclear. To investigate the associations of OSA with semen parameters, erectile function, and inflammatory profiles, and to assess longitudinal changes in these markers following continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. This prospective study enrolled 72 reproductive-aged men with OSA and 22 non-OSA controls. Polysomnography was performed at baseline only. During CPAP follow-up, treatment efficacy was ascertained from device-recorded hours of use and residual apnoea-hypopnoea index. Erectile function (IIEF-5), semen quality, and serum/seminal cytokines were assessed. Compared with controls, OSA patients showed significantly lower total and progressive sperm motility and semen volume, along with elevated seminal IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10, and IL-17A, without corresponding changes in serum cytokines or erectile function. During CPAP follow-up, adherent patients demonstrated early improvements in progressive sperm motility as early as 1 month post-treatment. Sleep architecture disruption and local seminal inflammation were independently associated with reduced semen quality. OSA is associated with reduced semen quality and localized seminal inflammation, without corresponding systemic or erectile changes. CPAP therapy is accompanied by longitudinal improvements in sperm motility, suggesting that evaluation for sleep-disordered breathing may be considered an exploratory assessment in men presenting with unexplained semen abnormalities.

papers.title: Reduction in reported nightmares during adjunctive trihexyphenidyl treatment in an adolescent: A case report.
papers.abstract: Nightmares are a frequent and disabling symptom of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and may perpetuate fear of sleep, insomnia, and psychiatric deterioration. Evidence for pharmacologic treatment in children and adolescents remains limited. We report a 13-year-old boy with PTSD who reported cessation of persistent nightmares during adjunctive trihexyphenidyl (THP) treatment. Polysomnography showed an apnea-hypopnea index of 9.4/h, with 24.5/h during rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. The patient and his family preferred to prioritize nightmare management and psychiatric care over treatment of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). THP was started at 1 mg nightly and increased to 2 mg after one week. At one-month follow-up, he reported no nightmares from the first treatment night, and sleep avoidance had resolved despite receiving no OSA treatment. Nightmares recurred within days of abrupt THP discontinuation. Although this course suggests a contribution of THP, we cannot determine whether nightmares ceased or continued without being recalled after awakening. Further studies are needed to clarify its efficacy, safety, dosing, and patient selection.

papers.title: Nrf2 protects against renal injury induced by chronic intermittent hypoxia via Nrf2/TrxR2 signaling pathway.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS), characterized by chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH), is associated with renal injury in pediatric populations. Nuclear factor E2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) is known to exert protective effects against oxidative stress, yet its role in CIH-induced renal damage remains unclear. This study aims to investigate whether Nrf2 protects against CIH-induced renal injury and to explore the involvement of the Nrf2/TrxR2 signaling pathway. C57BL/6 mice were exposed to CIH and treated with the Nrf2 agonist sulforaphane (SFN) or the inhibitor ATRA. In parallel, HK-2 renal tubular cells were subjected to CIH with Nrf2 or TrxR2 siRNA knockdown. Renal function, histopathology, oxidative stress markers, Nrf2 nuclear translocation, and downstream antioxidant protein expression were evaluated. Four weeks of CIH exposure significantly impaired renal function, as evidenced by elevated serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, and urinary β2-microglobulin levels. Histologically, CIH caused tubular epithelial cell swelling, luminal narrowing, and interstitial fibrosis. Nrf2 activation ameliorated these functional and structural abnormalities, while Nrf2 inhibition aggravated them. Mechanistically, Nrf2 activation enhanced its nuclear translocation and upregulated TrxR2 expression, accompanied by increased superoxide dismutase activity and decreased malondialdehyde levels. Nrf2 alleviates CIH-induced renal injury by suppressing oxidative stress through the Nrf2/TrxR2 signaling pathway, highlighting Nrf2 as a potential therapeutic target for OSAHS-related renal dysfunction.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG functional connectivity changes following memantine administration in children with autism spectrum disorder: an exploratory pre-post study.
papers.abstract: Despite the widespread use of memantine in modulating excitatory/inhibitory balance, the precise changes in the topology of brain networks following memantine administration in preschool children remain clearly undefined. The objective of this study is a quantitative evaluation of brain functional connectivity changes associated with memantine administration in using EEG-based network analysis. In this research, 22 preschool ASD children underwent treatment with memantine for one month. Resting-state electroencephalogram (EEG) signals were recorded before and after the intervention. functional connectivity matrices were extracted using the Phase Locking Value (PLV) index. Individual-level analysis revealed a Neurophysiological heterogeneity pattern, consisting of a 64% Subgroup with increased network integration (n = 14) with increased connectivity and 36% with decreased connectivity. SPN analysis identified distinct spatial components of network reorganization: (1) localized connectivity suppression in the fronto-central (Fz, F3) and left occipital (O1) regions captured by lower-order spatial filters, and (2) reinforcement of long-range functional coupling and enhanced nodal centrality in the right parietal (P4) and left temporal (T3) regions in higher-order filters. These findings suggest spatial network reorganization patterns associated with memantine administration, characterized by a complementary balance between localized phase decoupling and long-range functional integration.

papers.title: Sigma-1 receptor alleviates postoperative cognitive dysfunction exacerbated by preoperative acute sleep deprivation in mice via modulating the Keap1/Nrf2 signaling pathway.
papers.abstract: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) is a common neurological complication severely affecting patient prognosis. Preoperative acute sleep deprivation, a frequent perioperative stressor, significantly exacerbates POCD severity. Sigma-1 receptor (σ-1R), an endoplasmic reticulum molecular chaperone, plays a crucial role in modulating neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. However, whether σ-1R can serve as an interventional target to mitigate sleep deprivation-aggravated cognitive impairment remains insufficiently elucidated. This study aimed to clarify the regulatory role of σ-1R in a mouse model combining preoperative sleep deprivation with exploratory laparotomy, focusing on Keap1/Nrf2 signaling, and to evaluate its clinical translational potential. Behavioral, molecular biological, and morphological methods were utilized. Sleep deprivation exacerbated postoperative cognitive impairment, accompanied by a compensatory upregulation of σ-1R expression in hippocampal microglia. Notably, exogenous potentiation of σ-1R with the agonist PRE-084 reversed cognitive deficits, suppressed neuroinflammation and oxidative stress, promoted Nrf2 nuclear translocation, and upregulated downstream genes HO-1 and NQO1; conversely, the antagonist BD-1047 worsened the damage. Mechanistically, σ-1R physically associated with Keap1, promoting Nrf2 release. The Nrf2 inhibitor ML385 blocked PRE-084's protective effects. In vitro experiments confirmed PRE-084 alleviated inflammation and oxidative stress via an Nrf2-dependent pathway. Moreover, σ-1R signaling may partially contribute to the neuroprotective effects of dexmedetomidine. In conclusion, this study reveals that σ-1R activation is associated with protective effects in sleep deprivation-exacerbated POCD, potentially through regulating the Keap1/Nrf2 signaling pathway, a mechanism rarely reported in this context, suggesting σ-1R as a potential avenue for further investigation in POCD prevention.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Nightmare disorder and depression: Exploring a neglected clinical association" [J. Psychiatr. Res. 202, (2026), 127-136].
papers.abstract: Nightmares are overrepresented in psychiatric disorders and are strongly associated with suicidality, especially in Major Depressive Episode (MDE). This study had two main objectives: (1) to determine an optimal diagnostic cutoff for the Nightmare Severity Index (NSI) to identify Nightmare Disorder (ND), and (2) to compare the clinical profiles of MDE patients with ND (MDE-ND) and without ND (MDE-WND). We hypothesized that MDE-ND represents a more severe depressive subtype. This prospective case-control study was conducted in routine clinical settings. Participants were adults diagnosed with MDE according to DSM-5 criteria. Two groups were defined using NSI scores. The NSI cutoff score for diagnosing ND was determined using a Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve and the Youden Index. Psychiatric symptoms, sleep quality, and circadian rhythms were assessed using self-report questionnaires. Objective sleep and circadian rhythm parameters were measured using actigraphy. The NSI demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance with a cutoff ≥10 (sensitivity: 96.67%, specificity: 93.94%). Nearly half (49.6%) of MDE patients met ND criteria. Compared to MDE-WND, MDE-ND patients showed greater clinical severity, including higher lifetime and current suicidality and more severe depressive, anxiety, and insomnia symptoms. They exhibited longer sleep latency, poorer sleep continuity, and objectively lower sleep efficiency. Logistic regression identified anxiety severity, insomnia, and female gender as significant factors associated with ND. Mediation analyses revealed indirect associations within the tested models between nightmares and suicidality with anxiety mediating the link. MDE-ND is a more severe depressive subtype, with greater psychiatric burden and sleep disturbances. Early identification may help reduce suicidality by targeting nightmares in this high-risk group.

papers.title: [Perception, symptoms and management of menopause in Spanish women: results of an anonymous online survey].
papers.abstract: To describe the perceived impact of menopause on quality of life, symptom prevalence, and treatment use among Spanish women, based on the findings of an online survey conducted among women residing in Spain, promoted by the HM Foundation Chair in Menopause. An anonymous open online survey was conducted between January and June 2024. A total of 3,825 women aged 40-65 years participated. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics based on self-reported responses, 95% confidence intervals (Wilson method), and two-sided proportion tests against a 50% reference value. The mean age was 52.1±7.4 years, with an estimated BMI of 25.0kg/m2. Most participants were non-smokers (88.7%) and had an intact uterus (94.9%). The most frequent symptoms were sleep disturbances (84.1%), fatigue (80.5%), emotional changes (75.7%), cognitive difficulties (71.9%), and hot flashes (71.4%). A total of 79.8% reported a perceived negative impact on quality of life, and 70.1% reported moderate to severe productivity impairment. Only 12.0% were receiving menopausal hormone therapy (MHT), and 44.0% considered themselves well informed about menopause. The most commonly used medications were those for sleep or anxiety (21.6%) and cholesterol control (12.3%). Preventive screening rates were high (mammography 93.8%, Pap smear 91.2%). Despite the high prevalence of symptoms and good participation in preventive programs, the use of MHT remains low, while the uptake of specific non-hormonal therapeutic options, such as fezolinetant, remains limited. These findings highlight an information gap and underscore the relevance of sleep and emotional well-being to the perceived impact of menopause.

papers.title: Towards improving Alzheimer's intervention: a machine learning approach for biomarker detection through combining MEG and MRI pipelines.
papers.abstract: To identify robust biomarkers for early cognitive decline, classification performance was evaluated for healthy controls (HC) versus mild cognitive impairment (MCI) using MEG-derived spectral features at the sensor and source levels, and by testing whether adding MRI anatomical features improves discrimination in the BioFIND cohort. Data from 324 participants (166 HC and 158 MCI) were analyzed using automated artifact rejection and source reconstruction. Spectral biomarkers, including sensor-space and sourcespace representations, were extracted from the magnetometer and gradiometer signals. Five inverse-solution methods were assessed (including linearly constrained minimum variance [LCMV] and exact low-resolution electromagnetic tomography analysis [eLORETA]) to increase the robustness of source-based biomarker selection. Multiple classifiers, including a support vector machine (SVM) and L1-regularized logistic regression (GLMNET), were compared using nested K-fold cross-validation embedded in Monte Carlo replications to limit overfitting. The best performance was obtained by combining MRI features with source-based MEG features using GLMNET, achieving 76.31 ± 1.47% accuracy and 82.44 ± 1.44% AUC. MEG-only models showed strong discrimination and outperformed MRI-only analyses, particularly those based on the LCMV and eLORETA features. Across settings, the SVM and GLMNET were the most consistently effective classifiers. These findings support MEG/EEG spectral biomarkers, particularly source-based representations, as sensitive markers of early AD-related functional changes. Integrating MEG with MRI can further improve HC-versus-MCI classification. The study also demonstrated that rigorous validation (nested cross-validation with Monte Carlo replication) is essential for reliable biomarker assessment and for comparing preprocessing, inverse-solution, and classifier choices in translational neuroimaging pipelines.

papers.title: Motor cortex-based intracortical BCI performance is robust to changes in attentional load during dual-tasking.
papers.abstract: High performance intracortical brain-computer interface (iBCI) control has been demonstrated in research settings, but performance can still vary within and between sessions. One potential source of this variability is the change in attentional load that comes from processing naturally occurring distractors such as thoughts, sounds, fatigue, or pain. To improve the consistency of iBCI performance in real-world environments where this sort of multi-tasking is inevitable, we must understand how shifts in attention can impact performance. Approach: Here we examined the effect of attentional load on iBCI performance and movement-related neural activity using a 2D cursor translation + click iBCI task paired with an N-Back working memory task to increase attentional load during dual-task performance. Two participants (P2 and P4) with tetraplegia completed the study while enrolled in a long-term clinical trial of an iBCI device. Common neural correlates of attention (theta and alpha band power) were measured with simultaneously recorded scalp electroencephalography (EEG). Main Results: While the EEG metrics and difficulty ratings suggested increased attentional load during dual-tasking, iBCI performance was quite robust across the various dual-tasking conditions. One participant, P2, experienced a small but significant increase in trial completion time and normalized path length during the mild attentional load condition compared to the moderate load condition. Signal quality differences between the two participants may have impacted the results, as P2 had lower signal quality and was therefore likely more vulnerable to attentional load. P4's higher signal quality likely allowed him to accommodate increased attentional load without a drop in performance. Significance: Overall, iBCI performance appears to be robust to attentional load, but the complex trends observed here reflect a need for continued investigation of BCI use under different cognitive states to elucidate potential challenges and compensatory mechanisms across participants. &#xD.

papers.title: Cenobamate in Focal-Onset Refractory and Super-Refractory Status Epilepticus: A Multicenter Cohort Study With Matched Analysis.
papers.abstract: Cenobamate (CNB) is an antiseizure medication (ASM) with demonstrated efficacy in drug-resistant focal epilepsy, but its role in status epilepticus (SE) remains unclear. Emerging evidence suggests that it may achieve early clinically meaningful seizure control at relatively low doses, with an acceptable safety profile, supporting its potential utility as an urgent adjunctive therapy in severe refractory epilepsy. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of CNB for the treatment of focal-onset refractory SE (RSE) and super-refractory SE (SRSE) in real-world clinical practice. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using a prospectively maintained registry including adult patients with focal RSE and SRSE treated between January 2022 and October 2025. Clinical, EEG, and treatment data were collected. The primary outcome was sustained SE termination (>24 hours) with electroclinical resolution attributable to CNB. A secondary propensity score-matched analysis (1:2) compared CNB-exposed patients with matched nonexposed controls from the same registry (2011-2025), using target trial emulation principles. Thirty-one patients received CNB (mean age 61 ± 21 years; 54.8% male); 45.2% met criteria for SRSE. CNB was initiated a median of 4 days (interquartile range [IQR] 2-12) after SE onset after failure of 5 ASMs (IQR 4-5), at a median starting dose of 50 mg/d (IQR 25-50). Sustained SE resolution occurred in 26 patients (83.9%), including all patients with RSE (17/17) and 64.3% with SRSE. Response occurred after a median of 2 days (IQR 1-6). In the matched cohort analysis (28 CNB exposed vs 56 controls), SE resolution was higher in CNB-treated patients (82.1% vs 57.1%; p = 0.02). In multivariable analysis, CNB exposure was independently associated with SE resolution (adjusted odds ratio 5.9, 95% CI 1.2-30, p = 0.03). No serious CNB-related adverse events occurred. Mild adverse events were observed in 51.6%, most commonly somnolence. In-hospital mortality was 22.6% with no deaths attributed to CNB. In this multicenter real-world cohort, CNB was associated with high rates of sustained SE termination in RSE and SRSE and improved outcomes compared with matched controls, without serious safety signals. These findings support CNB as a potential adjunctive therapeutic option in refractory focal SE. This study provides Class IV evidence that CNB is effective as an adjunctive therapy for the control of focal-onset RSE and SRSE in adult patients.

papers.title: Real-World Health Monitoring Using Wrist-Worn Wearables in Community-Dwelling Older Adults in China: Mixed Methods Feasibility Study.
papers.abstract: Real-world behavioral and physiological functioning, including heart rate, daily mobility, and sleep patterns, may provide information about aging and early neurodegenerative changes that is not captured by periodic clinical visits. Wrist-worn wearable devices offer a promising approach for continuous, passive monitoring of these domains. However, evidence regarding feasibility, usability, and acceptability in real-world observational settings among community-dwelling older adults in China remains limited. This study primarily aimed to evaluate the feasibility, usability, and acceptability of using wrist-worn wearable devices to monitor behavioral and physiological function in community-dwelling older adults under naturalistic conditions. As a secondary objective, the study descriptively characterized wearable-derived behavioral and physiological measures among participants with minimal consecutive valid monitoring. We enrolled 486 community-dwelling older adults from the Beijing region of the China-Aging cohort, each of whom received a Huawei Band 8 commercial wrist-worn wearable device. A valid monitoring day was defined as 10 or more hours of wear time. Participants were classified into three monitoring-pattern categories based on predefined wear-time criteria: no valid monitoring day, nonconsecutive valid monitoring, and minimal consecutive valid monitoring (≥3 consecutive valid monitoring days). Demographic characteristics, health status, and cognitive and functional measures (Mini-Mental State Examination and Barthel Activities of Daily Living Index) were compared across groups. Usability, acceptability, and perceived barriers were assessed using a structured user experience survey. Of 486 participants, 224 (46.1%) achieved minimal consecutive valid monitoring, 156 (32.1%) had nonconsecutive valid monitoring, and 106 (21.8%) had no valid monitoring day. Self-rated health differed significantly across monitoring patterns (P=.005), whereas no significant differences were observed for the other measured baseline characteristics. Among participants with minimal consecutive valid monitoring, mean daily heart rate was 72.1 (SD 8.6) bpm, median daily step count was 6177 (IQR 4249-8872) steps/day, and sleep data were available for 211 out of 224 (94.2%), with a median sleep duration of 7.23 (IQR 6.48-8.04) hours. The user experience survey was completed by 106 out of 486 (21.8%) participants, with higher participation among those with more sustained monitoring. Respondents generally reported favorable usability and acceptability; common barriers included device discomfort, data synchronization issues, and battery life. Wrist-worn wearable monitoring was feasible under naturalistic conditions for a substantial proportion of community-dwelling older adults in China, with generally favorable usability and acceptability among survey respondents. However, monitoring patterns varied considerably across individuals, highlighting challenges for long-term use and large-scale implementation. These findings support the potential of wearable technologies for longitudinal monitoring outside clinic-based assessments. Further research is needed to establish the stability and clinical relevance of wearable-derived behavioral measures over longer monitoring periods.

papers.title: How we see relations: The case of containment and support.
papers.abstract: To navigate and act in the environment, it is necessary to recognize objects and the relationships between them. Recognition of objects in visual scenes is rapid and automatic. Are relations between objects in a scene also extracted rapidly and automatically during perception? Here, we considered containment and support, two relations that are fundamental to our understanding of the physical world. Using frequency-tagging electroencephalography on human subjects, we measured stimulus-driven neural responses during rapid visual presentation of images (4 Hz), with a periodic oddball structure to isolate the selective response to object pairs presented side-by-side (e.g., a book and a table) versus two objects in support or containment relations (e.g., a book on a table). We found enhanced responses to objects in support/containment relations (vs. objects side-by-side) when a relation was instantiated by different exemplars of the same scene (e.g., a book on a table), but not by different scenes involving distinct object categories (e.g., a book on a table, a lamp on a stand, a laptop on a desk). These findings indicate that, during scene perception, relations are extracted in a format that generalizes within, but not across, types of visual scenes. We propose that, during perception, relations are not represented as discrete, abstract tokens ("in" or "on") but rather as objects' properties, such that changes in the objects entail changes in the relational representation. These results provide new insight into the perceptual foundations of relational processing underlying physical reasoning. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Validation of a Four-Extrastimulus Ventricular Stimulation Protocol for Arrhythmic Risk Stratification in Tetralogy of Fallot.
papers.abstract: Risk stratification for sustained ventricular arrhythmias (SVA) in adults with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) remains challenging. Although programmed ventricular stimulation (PVS) has shown a high negative predictive value, the prognostic performance of a four-extrastimulus PVS protocol-validated in ischemic heart disease-has not been systematically evaluated in congenital heart disease. We retrospectively included 41 consecutive adults with repaired TOF who underwent EPS using a standardized four-extrastimulus PVS protocol at two right ventricular sites. Inducibility of SVA was assessed. The primary endpoint was the occurrence of clinical SVA during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Firth-penalized Cox regression were used to evaluate prognostic performance, and diagnostic accuracy metrics were calculated. Inducibility was observed in 18 patients (44%). During a median follow-up of 1.68 years, SVA occurred exclusively in inducible patients (5/18; 28%), all corresponding to sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. No non-inducible patient developed SVA. Inducibility was associated with significantly lower SVA-free survival (log-rank p = 0.015) and an increased risk of events (HR 13.6; 95% CI 1.5-1804; p = 0.017) in univariate analysis. The four-extrastimulus protocol demonstrated a sensitivity of 100% and specificity of 64%. In adults with repaired TOF and risk factors for sudden cardiac death, the four-extrastimulus PVS protocol identified a subgroup at high arrhythmic risk while reliably excluding events in non-inducible individuals. These findings support the potential value of PVS as part of multimodal risk stratification, particularly for identifying patients in whom ICD implantation may be deferred.

papers.title: Understanding Glymphatic's Role In Proteinopathies (GRIP): A single centre case-control study protocol.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) are proteinopathies characterized by pathological accumulation of amyloid beta, phosphorylated-tau, and alpha-synuclein. Impaired clearance of these proteins is thought to contribute to disease pathogenesis, whereas preserved or enhanced clearance may be compensatory. Beyond intracellular degradation within neurons and glial cells, an extracellular clearance pathway, the glymphatic system, facilitates cerebrospinal fluid flow into perivascular spaces, exchange with interstitial fluid, and subsequent clearance from the brain. Glymphatic transport may therefore be critical for removal of excess proteins and metabolic waste, and its dysfunction could promote protein aggregation and neurodegeneration. The Glymphatic's Role In Proteinopathies (GRIP) study is an observational case-control imaging and biomarker study comparing glymphatic clearance in patients with AD, PD, and DLB versus healthy controls. We aim to recruit 70 participants: PD (n = 20), DLB (n = 10), AD (n = 20), and age- and sex-matched healthy controls (n = 20). The AD group will be stratified by pathology, with half amyloid-positive/tau-negative (A + T-) and half amyloid- and tau-positive (A + T+). The PD group will be stratified by disease duration. Participants will undergo baseline MRI followed by intrathecal injection of gadobutrol (0.25 mmol) and serial MRI at 5, 24, 48, and 72 hours. Influx and efflux of tracer will be modeled from T1 signal changes. Blood will be sampled repeatedly from 1 to 72 hours; cerebrospinal fluid will be collected at baseline. Individual glymphatic clearance will be estimated using population pharmacokinetic methods, where gadobutrol serves as a tracer. Sleep will be monitored with triaxial accelerometry and sleep diaries. The primary outcome is group differences in glymphatic clearance metrics between each disease group and controls; secondary analyses will explore associations with cognition, disease severity and duration, sleep quality, and cerebrospinal fluid protein levels.

papers.title: Prevalence and factors associated with excessive daytime somnolence in adults with HIV - A single-centre UK observational study.
papers.abstract: IntroductionExcessive daytime somnolence is common in people with HIV. The importance of possible contributors such as mental health and obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome is poorly understood. We investigated the prevalence of daytime somnolence and obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome in people with HIV in the UK and assessed what factors were associated with somnolence.MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, adults with HIV attending Royal Free London HIV outpatient service appointments were recruited between May 2018 to October 2019. Participants completed questionnaires as outpatients assessing somnolence, sleep quality, fatigue, mental health symptoms and quality of life. Binary logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with excessive daytime somnolence (defined as Epworth Sleepiness Scale scores >10/24), and prevalence of somnolence and obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome were calculated with 95% confidence intervals.Results313 adults (median age 52 years, body mass index (BMI) 25.9 kg/m2, and 80% male) participated. The excessive daytime somnolence prevalence was 72/313 (23%, 95% CI: 18.5-28.1). Somnolent individuals had more frequent and more severe: anxiety, depression, fatigue and poor sleep quality, with more reported cardiovascular and respiratory disease (p < 0.01). Factors independently associated with excessive somnolence included male gender (OR 3.45; 1.36-8.95; p < 0.01), poor sleep quality (OR 1.12; 1.02-1.22; p = 0.01) and fatigue (OR 1.04; 1.01-1.06; p < 0.01). The minimum detected prevalence of obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome was 8.6% (n = 27/313) in the study population - which represented 54% (n = 27/50) of those participants who had a sleep study.ConclusionsExcessive daytime somnolence is common in people with HIV and frequently identified in individuals reporting poor mental health. Obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome is a potentially treatable contributor to daytime somnolence. Integrated screening for somnolence, sleep disorders and mental health within routine HIV care may improve identification and treatment of common, modifiable and interacting comorbidities.

papers.title: Association Between Circadian Rhythm Sleep Disorder and Noninfectious Uveitis: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Circadian misalignment influences ocular immune homeostasis, inflammatory signaling, and blood-retinal barrier integrity, each implicated in the pathogenesis of noninfectious uveitis (NIU). Whether clinically diagnosed circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder (CRSD) is associated with incident NIU is unknown. This study examined that association in a large multicenter cohort. This retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX federated network. Adults with CRSD (ICD-10 G47.2) were compared with adults who underwent polysomnography without a sleep disorder. Patients with uveitis before the index date or with causes of infectious or secondary intraocular inflammation were excluded. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) for incident anterior and composite NIU, adjusting for demographics, systemic comorbidities, corticosteroid exposure, and prior ophthalmology encounters. Major depressive disorder and appendicitis served as positive and negative control outcomes. The CRSD cohort included 47 323 adults and the comparator cohort 22 241 adults. CRSD was independently associated with an increased hazard of incident anterior NIU (aHR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.11-2.61) and composite NIU (aHR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.21-2.79). Control outcomes performed as expected, with a strong association for major depressive disorder (aHR, 2.19; 95% CI, 2.10-2.29) and no association for appendicitis (aHR, 1.12; 95% CI, 0.87-1.45). Clinically diagnosed CRSD was independently associated with an increased risk of incident NIU. These findings support a potential role for circadian dysregulation in ocular inflammatory disease and warrant prospective confirmation.

papers.title: Sleep after motor learning enhances post-movement beta synchronization.
papers.abstract: The neural substrates supporting the beneficial effect of sleep on motor memory consolidation are well described. However, less is known about brain oscillatory dynamics underlying these processes. We characterized the oscillatory dynamics associated with motor sequence learning and their modulation by post-learning sleep using magnetoencephalography (MEG) in young healthy adults. After learning a motor sequence task while their brain activity was recorded with MEG, participants were distributed in two groups according to whether they slept or were totally sleep deprived during the first post-training night. Consolidation was assessed with a retest in the MEG three days later. Behaviorally, performance improved over the consolidation interval irrespective of whether sleep was afforded during the first night. MEG results showed that initial motor sequence learning was characterized by a decrease in beta event-related desynchronization (ERD, 18 to 25 Hz) over bilateral motor areas from early to late training. Interestingly, while practice-related modulations of beta ERD were not influenced by the sleep status, post-learned-movement beta event-related synchronization (ERS) over bilateral parietal areas increased over the consolidation interval in the sleep, compared to the sleep deprived, group. These results extend current models of motor memory consolidation by identifying ERS as an oscillatory marker of sleep-dependent consolidation.

papers.title: Sleep neurophysiology as a biological correlate of infant temperament.
papers.abstract: Temperament, characterized as individual differences in reactivity and self-regulation, influences our behavior in everyday situations. It is apparent as early as infancy and shaped by genetic and environmental factors. A neurophysiological marker of temperament has been quantified during the waking state; however, it remains unknown how these associations manifest in sleep. To address this gap, we assessed nighttime sleep in 29 6-month-old infants (Mage = 6.145 months, SD = 0.399, 48% males) using a portable high-density electroencephalography. Temperament was assessed using a parent-rated questionnaire, focusing on 2 scales: negative affectivity and orienting/regulatory capacity. The correlation analyses included: (i) frontal asymmetry and (ii) whole-brain, electrode-wise correlations with temperament. The predefined frontal asymmetry correlation revealed that increased left-hemispheric slow-wave activity (SWA) corresponded to higher orienting/regulatory capacity scores. The whole-brain correlation showed that higher theta power across an array of electrodes over the prefrontal regions was associated with decreased negative affectivity scores. Local sleep depth over frontal and temporal brain areas, as reflected by SWA asymmetry and theta power, serves as a marker of self-regulatory abilities and affective traits, which, in turn, reflect differences in temperament. Our findings reveal that sleep neurophysiology is a biological correlate of temperament during preverbal stages.

papers.title: Robust Epilepsy Diagnosis in Neonates Via Spatio-Temporal Graph Learning and Balanced Test-Time Training.
papers.abstract: Timely diagnosis of neonatal epilepsy is critical for mitigating long-term neurodevelopmental deficits. However, while neonates exhibiting extensive seizure burden are readily identified, accurately diagnosing epileptic infants with sparse or no overt seizure onset during monitoring remains a formidable challenge using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals alone. Current automated systems predominantly target ictal-specific seizure detection, limiting their clinical utility for risk stratification during seizure-free intervals (interictal), particularly given the pronounced EEG variability across neonates. This work presents a cross-subject deep learning framework that robustly distinguishes epileptic from "healthy" neonates by integrating dynamic graph topology with self-supervised adaptation. Our architecture models multichannel EEG as spatio-temporal graphs to capture functional connectivity, while a balanced test-time training mechanism dynamically adapts the model to unseen patients via masked signal reconstruction. This effectively mitigates the domain shifts caused by inter-subject variability without requiring patient-specific labels. Validated on a clinically curated cohort of 140 neonates (70 healthy, 70 epileptic), our approach achieves a segment-level accuracy of 83$\%$ and an area under the curve of 0.90. For the primary subject-level endpoint, accuracy increases from 0.79 without adaptation to 0.88 with balanced TTT, using aggregation thresholds selected on inner validation subjects and fixed before evaluation on each held-out fold. The cohort includes anoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, benign neonatal convulsions, and cerebrovascular accident. Analyses restricted to non-ictal windows also support discrimination between the two groups, although all neonates in the epilepsy group experienced seizures elsewhere in their recordings.

papers.title: GeoMind: Dancing with Geometric Brain Rhythm on Symmetric Positive Definite Manifolds.
papers.abstract: State space model (SSM) is a powerful tool in neuroscience field to characterize the dynamic nature of brain functions by elucidating the mechanism of how brain system transits between brain states and how underlying states give rise to the observed neural activities. Although tremendous efforts have been made to lend the power of deep learning and mathematical insight of SSM in various functional neuroimaging studies, current state-of-the-art methods lack a holistic view of brain state evolution as a self-organized dynamical system where each part of the brain is functionally inter-connected. Since the topological co-activation of functional fluctuations exhibits an intrinsic geometric pattern (symmetric and positive definite, SPD) on the Riemannian manifold, the call for understanding how a selective set of functional connectivities in the brain supports diverse behavior and cognition emerge a new machine learning scenario of manifold-based SSM for largescale functional neuroimages. To that end, we propose a geometric neural network of SSM, coined GeoMind, designed to uncover evolving brain states by tracking the trajectory of functional dynamics on a high-dimensional Riemannian manifold of SPD matrices. GeoMind demonstrates promising results in identifying specific brain states on task-based functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) data, as well as in diseases early diagnosis for Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease and Autism, by using resting-state fMRI. These results highlight the applicability of GeoMind in neuroscience research. To further evaluate generalizability of GeoMind, we applied GeoMind to electroencephalography (EEG) emotion datasets, outperforming competing methods and demonstrating scalability across neuroimaging modalities.

papers.title: Auditory Attention Decoding from Low Spatial Resolution Ring-Ear Wearable Electrodes: Implications for Intelligent Hearing Aids.
papers.abstract: High-density cap-EEG has achieved strong performance in auditory attention decoding (AAD), but its bulkiness and complexity limit its use in wearable applications such as daily-use hearing aids. Ring-ear wearable electrodes (cEEGrid) offer a promising alternative. However, their low spatial resolution poses significant challenges for reliable decoding, especially under short decision windows. In this study, we investigate whether auditory attention can be directly decoded from low-resolution periauricular electrophysiological signals recorded by cEEGrid, without relying on external audio information. To this end, we propose a lightweight neural network, cEEGridNet, designed for ring-ear recordings, and adopt an attention guidance protocol that better reflects realistic listening conditions. With a 1000 ms decision window, the proposed approach achieved left-right spatial auditory attention decoding accuracies of 64.90% and 62.92% under cross-trial and cross-subject validation, respectively. cEEGridNet outperformed the baseline models under both validation settings, but its generalization to unseen trials and unseen subjects remained limited. Challenges also remain in timbre-based attention decoding, and possible gaze-related contributions cannot be excluded.

papers.title: Cross-Domain Slow Wave Sleep Detection from Single-Lead EEG in Pediatric Congenital Heart Disease Recovery.
papers.abstract: Slow wave sleep (SWS) is vital for neural recovery and cardiovascular stability in children following congenital heart disease (CHD) surgery. However, pediatric CHD sleep patterns are often disrupted by clinical stressors and exhibit substantial domain discrepancies relative to adult data distributions. To address these challenges, this study establishes the Pediatric Cardiac Post-surgical Sleep (PCPS) dataset, a self-collected and expert-annotated pediatric polysomnography (PSG) dataset specifically targeting the early post-CHD surgical period. We further propose PCPS-SleepNet, an end-to-end deep learning framework for cross-domain sleep staging from single-lead EEG, enabling effective knowledge transfer from public sleep data to pediatric post-surgical CHD data. The architecture employs a multi-band input representation across six sub-bands and leverages a Four-Stage Progressive Encoder integrating Multi-Scale Depthwise Convolution (MSDC) for local features, self-attention for global density modeling, and a Conformer block for hybrid refinement. To mitigate limited pediatric data availability and domain shift, this network is pre-trained on public datasets and fine-tuned on the PCPS dataset. Subject-independent validation showed competitive performance, with an overall accuracy of 75.65 ± 0.58%, an AUROC of 89.06 ± 0.18%, an AUPRC of 83.49 ± 0.13%, and a macro F1-score of 76.68 ± 0.70%. For SWS detection, the model achieved an AUPRC of 87.89 ± 0.20% and an F1-score of 81.55 ± 0.74%. Architectural ablations and frequency-band input contribution analysis supported the model design and suggested the complementary discriminative value of slow-wave frequency-band inputs. These results suggest a practical and patient-friendly sleep detection solution for individualized sleep assessment and rehabilitation in vulnerable pediatric populations.

papers.title: Full-Spectrum Spectroscopic Characterization of Extracellular pH Effects on FRET-Based Genetic Voltage Indicators Expressed in Xenopus laevis Oocytes.
papers.abstract: Genetically encoded voltage indicators convert voltage-dependent conformational transitions of membrane proteins into optical signals. pH sensitivity is a critical yet often under-characterized property and becomes particularly important when extending imaging to organellar membranes. This chapter presents a step-by-step protocol for full-spectrum spectroscopic analysis of extracellular pH effects on FRET-based voltage indicators expressed in Xenopus laevis oocytes, beginning with assembly and alignment of the measurement rig. Oocytes enable real-time, full-spectrum spectroscopic measurements within a single cell under stable electrophysiological control, providing well-defined mechanistic characterization under conditions difficult to achieve in other systems.

papers.title: Impact of burst suppression duration on delirium and its diagnostic value in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
papers.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) delirium affects up to 50% of mechanically ventilated patients. This condition is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Although bispectral index (BIS) monitoring is widely used for sedation assessment, its predictive value for delirium remains limited. Burst suppression (BS) is an electroencephalographic pattern reflecting profound cerebral dysfunction. BS has been proposed as a predictor of delirium. However, the quantitative role of burst suppression duration (BSD) in delirium risk stratification has not been established. This prospective observational study enrolled 300 mechanically ventilated adult ICU patients between April 2021 and October 2024 at Harrison International Peace Hospital. Continuous video-electroencephalogram (vEEG) monitoring was performed. BSD was quantified from the vEEG recordings. Delirium was assessed using the Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU (CAM-ICU). Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent risk factors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of BSD. Among 300 patients, 130 (43.3%) developed delirium. The delirium group had significantly longer BSD than the control group (median 81.1 s, IQR 41.5-148.5 vs. 17.2 s, IQR 5.8-32.9; P < 0.001). Multivariate analysis identified BSD (adjusted OR = 1.018, 95% CI 1.012-1.023; P < 0.001), BIS (adjusted OR = 0.964, 95% CI 0.946-0.982; P < 0.001), age (adjusted OR = 1.024, 95% CI 1.002-1.047; P = 0.031), and hypertension (adjusted OR = 1.748, 95% CI 1.002-3.051; P = 0.049) as independent risk factors. ROC analysis demonstrated that BSD achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.871 (95% CI 0.829-0.913). The optimal cutoff of 41.5 s yielded a sensitivity of 80.8% and a specificity of 78.2%. The combination of BSD and BIS improved the AUC to 0.914 (95% CI 0.882-0.946). BSD is an independent risk factor for delirium in mechanically ventilated ICU patients. It demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy as a quantitative biomarker. The combination of BSD and BIS provides superior predictive performance. This combined approach offers a practical quantitative tool for early delirium risk stratification.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing

papers.title: A randomised controlled crossover trial comparing two mandibular repositioning appliances for treatment of moderate obstructive sleep apnoea.
papers.abstract: To compare two custom-made bi-block mandibular repositioning appliances, the SomnoDent® Flex and the OrthoApnea NOA®, in adults with moderate obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA). Randomised two-period, two-sequence crossover trial at a single centre (Genk, Belgium). Adults with polysomnography-confirmed AHI 5-30 events/h were eligible; all enrolled had moderate OSA (AHI 15.1-29.7). Participants were randomised 1:1 to SomnoDent® Flex-NOA® or the reverse sequence, each worn for three months with a two-week washout. Participants and clinicians were unblinded; outcome scorers were blinded to appliance. The registered primary outcome was the change in AHI from baseline for each appliance. The between-appliance difference in post-treatment AHI was assessed in a non-prespecified principal comparative analysis using linear mixed-effects models with appliance, period and sequence as fixed effects. Sixteen participants were randomised, eight per sequence, and all were analysed. Median AHI fell from 17.6 events/h at baseline to 3.1 with the SomnoDent® Flex and 2.3 with the NOA® (both p < 0.001 versus baseline). The between-appliance difference was + 0.16 events/h (95% CI - 2.56 to + 2.87; p = 0.904), with a period effect (+ 3.82 events/h in period 2, coinciding with the change from home polygraphy to in-laboratory polysomnography; p = 0.009). No secondary outcome differed significantly; post hoc, AHI < 5 events/h was reached in 12/16 (SomnoDent® Flex) and 10/16 (NOA®). No participant discontinued for an adverse event; adverse events were not systematically recorded. Both appliances were associated with reductions in AHI. The non-prespecified between-appliance comparison detected no statistically significant difference and does not establish equivalence. Complete confounding between period and measurement methodology, together with insufficient adherence, titration and adverse-event data, limits conclusions about the overall comparative merits of the appliances. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06810479, registered 5 February 2025, prior to first enrolment.

papers.title: Effects of Mobile-Based Multicomponent Infant Sleep Intervention on Infants and Mothers: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of a mobile-based multicomponent infant sleep intervention on infant and maternal sleep and maternal mental health. In this single-blind randomized controlled trial, mother-infant dyads with infants aged 3-12 months were recruited from an online parenting community in South Korea; 32 dyads were randomized and 29 were analyzed. From February to May 2021, the intervention group used a mobile application for 4 weeks providing infant sleep education, sleep monitoring, and personalized support. Sleep was assessed by actigraphy for 5 consecutive days at baseline, post-intervention (6 weeks), and follow-up (10 weeks). Maternal depression, fatigue, and sleep disturbance were assessed using the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System. Linear mixed-effects models examined group differences over time. Compared with the control group, infants in the intervention group showed greater improvements from baseline in sleep efficiency and wake after sleep onset at 6 and 10 weeks and in average awake time at 10 weeks. Mothers in the intervention group showed greater improvements in sleep efficiency, wake after sleep onset, and number of awakenings at 10 weeks. They also had a greater decrease in depression scores at 10 weeks and a difference in sleep disturbance scores favoring the intervention at 6 weeks, whereas fatigue did not differ between groups. A mobile-based, family-centered multicomponent sleep intervention was associated with greater improvements in selected infant and maternal sleep outcomes and maternal depression scores. Future studies should evaluate the long-term effectiveness and stability of these effects. This study was registered with the Clinical Research Information Service, a member of the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (KCT0005283), registered on August 4, 2020 ( https://cris.nih.go.kr/cris/search/detailSearch.do?seq=22693&search_page=L ).

papers.title: Combined vitamins C and E attenuate memory impairment and hippocampal damage in diabetic sleep-deprived mice: behavioral and molecular insights.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) and sleep disturbances are associated with cognitive impairment and hippocampal dysfunction, potentially involving oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. This study investigated the effects of vitamins C and E, individually and in combination, to determine whether their complementary antioxidant properties provide enhanced neuroprotective effects against cognitive and hippocampal alterations in diabetic sleep-deprived mice. Diabetes was induced in male BALB/c mice (25-30 g) by streptozotocin (60 mg/kg), followed by partial sleep deprivation using the inverted flowerpot method. Animals received vitamin C (50 mg/kg), vitamin E (100 mg/kg), or their combination for 20 days. Body weight and blood glucose were monitored. Spatial learning and memory were evaluated using the Morris water maze. Hippocampal histopathology, GFAP immunostaining, and expression of genes related to oxidative stress, inflammation, and neuroprotection were assessed. Vitamin E and combined vitamin C and E treatment reduced FBG and were associated with higher final body weight than untreated diabetic sleep-deprived mice. Vitamin treatments improved spatial learning and memory, with combined treatment producing greater improvements in selected behavioral outcomes. Combined treatment increased hippocampal neuronal density and reduced GFAP immunoreactivity. Vitamin treatment increased BDNF, Nrf2, and HO-1 expression and reduced iNOS, TNF-α, and IL-1β expression. Vitamin C and E, particularly in combination, were associated with improved metabolic, cognitive, and hippocampal outcomes in diabetic sleep-deprived mice, potentially involving modulation of neuroinflammatory and oxidative stress-related markers.
papers.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences

papers.title: The role of DISE and simulation bite in the selection of non-CPAP treatment modalities in patients with OSA.
papers.abstract: This study aims to investigate the role of drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) as a predictor of success of mandibular repositioning appliances (MRA), tonsillectomy and modified uvulopalatopharyngoplasty (mUPPP). Furthermore, the potential benefit of the use of a simulation bite during DISE is evaluated. A retrospective study was performed on 82 obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) patients unwilling or not tolerating continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) treatment. Patients with large tonsils were offered tonsillectomy and were excluded from the study. Nasal pathology was treated before possible inclusion in the study. All patients underwent DISE with chin lift or simulation bite to predict the effect of MRA, mUPPP and tonsillectomy and underwent a post-treatment polysomnography (PSG) afterwards. Of the 56 patients that were advised to start treatment with MRA and underwent post-treatment PSG, 96% achieved success. Only 4 patients underwent tonsillectomy and 7 underwent mUPPP, both with lower success rates (50% and 29% respectively). There was no difference in success rates of MRA between patients undergoing DISE with simulation bite or chin lift. The study confirms that DISE is an excellent predictor of MRA success. The success rate of mUPPP or tonsillectomy in cases of small tonsils is much lower than that of MRA and DISE is a less effective predictor of success for these surgical procedures.The value of using a simulation bite during DISE cannot be confirmed by this study. An adequately applied chin lift seems to predict the therapeutic effect of MRA as well as the use of a simulation bite.

papers.title: Wearable Technologies in Gastrointestinal Disorders: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
papers.abstract: Gastrointestinal disorders fluctuate between clinical encounters, creating a need for objective longitudinal monitoring. We review wearable technologies across gastrointestinal disorders, emphasizing clinical applications, current evidence, and barriers to implementation. Wearables capture physiologic, biochemical, and acoustic signals relevant to gastrointestinal disease. In inflammatory bowel disease, wearable-derived physiologic changes may precede inflammatory and symptomatic flares and help distinguish inflammatory from non-inflammatory symptoms. Sweat biosensors can measure inflammatory analytes, including calprotectin. Beyond inflammatory bowel disease, autonomic measures characterize disorders of gut-brain interaction, electrogastrographic and acoustic devices assess gastrointestinal motility, and activity and sleep metrics may aid postoperative recovery assessment and risk stratification in chronic liver disease. Evidence remains predominantly observational, and validated clinical thresholds are lacking, limiting the current clinical applicability of wearable derived signals. Wearables enable continuous, noninvasive monitoring across gastrointestinal disorders, but prospective trials are needed to establish clinical utility, actionable thresholds, workflow integration, and patient-centered implementation, and demonstrate improvement in clinically meaningful outcomes.

papers.title: Changes in obstructive sleep apnea severity, upper-airway findings, and health-related quality of life after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: a prospective before-and-after study.
papers.abstract: To evaluate changes in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, upper-airway findings, daytime sleepiness, and health-related quality of life approximately 6 months after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass in adults with obesity. We conducted a prospective single-group before-and-after study at Hospital de San José, Bogotá, Colombia. Adults with OSA undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass as routine care had pre- and postoperative polysomnography, anthropometric and otolaryngologic assessment, nasofibrolaryngoscopy, and patient-reported measures. Study eligibility required preoperative AHI > 5 events/h. Paired outcomes were analyzed with paired t, Wilcoxon signed-rank, or exact McNemar tests as appropriate. Of 33 patients assessed, 30 underwent surgery and 18 completed both objective evaluations. Mean weight decreased from 104.4 ± 12.6 to 68.5 ± 8.9 kg, BMI from 38.77 ± 4.94 to 25.82 ± 4.28 kg/m², and AHI from 23.70 ± 8.67 to 8.74 ± 4.35 events/h; mean AHI change was - 14.96 events/h (95% CI - 18.69 to - 11.22; p < 0.001). Residual OSA (AHI ≥ 5 events/h) persisted in 15/18 participants (83.3%; exact 95% CI 58.6-96.4%). Several upper-airway, sleepiness, and quality-of-life measures also changed favorably. Among participants with complete follow-up, Roux-en-Y gastric bypass was followed by lower OSA severity and favorable secondary outcomes, but complete remission was uncommon. Continued postoperative sleep reassessment remains important. Not applicable. This is an observational beforeandafter cohort study no health intervention was prospectively assigned for research purposes.

papers.title: [Neurostimulation in the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea].
papers.abstract: One of the most common sleep-related breathing disorders is obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), which is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity. Pathophysiologically, OSA is caused by collapse of the upper airway due to a sleep-induced reduction in muscle tone. The gold standard treatment is continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy; however, due to limited adherence , it is insufficient as the sole treatment for some patients. Hypoglossal nerve stimulation (HGNS) as an alternative treatment aims to activate the protrusion muscles of the tongue, thereby stabilizing the airway. Clinical studies show a significant reduction in the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) and an improvement in daytime symptoms even in long-term data. A prerequisite for therapeutic success is careful and thorough patient selection.

papers.title: Clinical and Psychological Impact of Pruritus Related to Skin Barrier Damage.
papers.abstract: Many external and internal factors can affect skin lipid synthesis and composition, which may impair skin barrier function, and potentially cause skin dryness, pruritus and other sensory symptoms. Pruritus, frequently associated with xerosis-particularly in inflammatory skin diseases, such as atopic dermatitis (AD)-is a commonly reported dermatological symptom in the general population. This narrative review, based on conference proceedings from clinicians and dermatologists, discusses the clinical and psychological impact of pruritus on individuals experiencing this subjective symptom. Starting with a summary of the key mechanisms involved in the itch-scratch cycle and signaling pathways shared with pain sensation, this review highlights the significant impact of chronic pruritus and associated symptoms, including sleep disturbances, on quality of life (QoL) and mental health. One of the main conclusions emerging from discussions between experts was that pruritus is a symptom with strong psychological features, which can easily become chronic under stressful conditions, and significantly affect patients' daily life and well-being. Therefore, the psychological issues associated with chronic pruritus, such as anxiety and depression, must not be overlooked, and dermatologists should perform a general psychodermatological assessment of patients with chronic pruritus for effective management of their dermatological and underlying psychological symptoms according to current guidelines. Management options need to include supportive skincare products and medical approaches to relieve symptoms of skin barrier dysfunction and chronic inflammation, as well as holistic strategies to help manage the psychological consequences of chronic pruritus. If concomitant psychopathologies are diagnosed, tailored drug treatments should be considered on a case-by-case basis to adequately address them.

papers.title: A consistency criterion for EQ-5D-5L bolt-on valuation.
papers.abstract: EuroQol is developing the EQ-5D Bolt-on Toolbox, an experimental set of bolt-ons designed to improve the sensitivity of EQ-5D-5L in specific populations. For use in cost-utility analyses, EQ-5D-5L+bolt-on value sets should be consistent with EQ-5D-5L value sets. This study proposes a method to define and maintain such consistency and examines its properties. We developed a novel contraction method that defines consistency using the distribution of disutilities in measurement data and estimates a contraction parameter from the conditional distribution of bolt-on levels given the core EQ-5D-5L profile to account for information overlap.
